## Persistence, publication and read contract

1. New Postgres migration: `financial_assumption_revision` with UUID ID, tenant/Site FK (Site required in this slice), stable key `diesel_price_per_litre`, revision number, ISO currency, unit `currency/L`, explicitly authored nonnegative finite `numeric`/Decimal value, basis enum `AUTHORED_ESTIMATE|CONTRACT_RATE|RECORDED_PURCHASE`, source reference, authored `[valid_from,valid_to)` intent, server `recorded_at`, server actor kind/id, nullable human `author_id`, channel, authorization basis, service/job/fixture provenance and idempotency key. Unique `(tenant_id,site_id,key,revision_no)` and publication key. No tenant fallback, default price, negative rate, SCENARIO operational publication, or client-supplied actor/author. The price value/basis/source and authored validity are immutable. Record effective validity separately as assignment rows keyed to the price revision with `[valid_from,valid_to)` and `[recorded_from,recorded_to)`. Assignment rows are immutable except a set-once `recorded_to` (trigger-enforced, as `foundation_revision.superseded_at`). Constraint: `EXCLUDE USING gist (tenant_id WITH =, site_id WITH =, assumption_key WITH =, tstzrange(valid_from,valid_to,'[)') WITH &&, tstzrange(recorded_from,recorded_to,'[)') WITH &&)`. Superseded and new rows share one server instant (`recorded_to` = `recorded_from`), taken with `clock_timestamp()` after acquiring the series lock (not transaction-start `now()`); it must be later than the series' latest `recorded_from`, and every stored range must be non-empty (CHECK `valid_from < valid_to` where bounded, and `recorded_from < recorded_to` when set). A trigger (it spans two tables, so not a CHECK) requires every current assignment's valid range to lie inside its revision's authored range. Index both time axes. A future publication closes the old assignment at `t` and retains its original revision ID for earlier time. A middle-only correction supersedes the old assignment, records two current assignments of the **same old price revision** for the unaffected left/right spans, and assigns the corrected middle to the new revision. Historical assignments remain selectable at older recorded cutoffs. Thus a price row is never rewritten, a pinned consequence still finds its original price ID, and `STALE` arises only if the price revision selected for its entire window actually changes. This assignment table is the migration's explicit resolution of review carry M1 and the technical design's simplified single validity row.
2. Publish only from a server-side CLI/job/fixture with a stable service principal, explicit Site, source, expected prior revision and idempotency key. The CLI is an administrative demo trigger, not an anonymous UI action; record SYSTEM/job/fixture provenance. Each publication carries a stored `change_kind`, shown in History. `INITIAL`: the first price for a Site/key, or one covering time with no current price; it may be backdated, and is refused with 409 if its range overlaps any current assignment. `SUCCESSION`: `valid_from` â‰¥ the server `recorded_at`; it may only truncate the single open-ended current assignment containing `valid_from`; any other overlap is refused with a typed 409. `CORRECTION`: backdated or bounded; requires a reason; supersedes the current assignments over its authored range and re-assigns the uncovered left/right remainders to their same old revisions. The transaction locks the Site/key series, rejects concurrent prior mismatch and conflicting retry payload, and returns the same revision ID on exact retry. After the transaction no two current assignments overlap (enforced by the item 1 constraint), and an overlap that `change_kind` does not permit is refused. S4-02a builds the human write route with no success path. Refusal order: 401 (no verified principal; the default access), then 422 (any body actor or author field), then 403/404 (tests inject these via the access seam); an admitted request without a verified human principal returns 401. It must not use `development_access`.
3. `GET /api/sites/{site_code}/financial-assumptions?key=&valid_at=&recorded_at=&after_revision_no=&limit=` and `/financial-assumptions/{revision_id}` (equivalent Site-scoped routes acceptable) return exact current/at-recorded-cutoff selection, selected ID, bounded pagination/cursor, valid and recorded intervals, price/currency/unit, basis/source, actor/channel/provenance and explicit no-price or conflict/source-failure state. Half-open boundary: a price ending at `t` does not cover `t`; another beginning at `t` does. An exact ID is stable after later writes. Reuse Finding API's tenant/Site 401/403/404 and 503 semantics; a bad/foreign revision never falls back to latest. Never promise arbitrary S3 `knowledge_at` replay: the cutoff selects stored assumption knowledge only.
4. The selected Finding route/Financials bridge holds Finding ID and exact FindingRevision ID, selected window and accepted-lineage link to S4-03. Before `fuel-cost-1` exists, display `QUANTITY_UNAVAILABLE`; when a separately supported technical quantity exists but no whole-window price, display `UNPRICED` with null amount/currency. These are typed states, not zero and not mock numbers. No consequence revision is manufactured in this slice. Closed Performance gate and pinned historical Finding follow S4-03 audit rules.

# S4-02b â€” bounded fuel consequence and repricing

Status: done (owner S4-02 checkpoint passed 2026-10-14, recorded conditional; reviews ACCEPT; merged to main by coordinator)
USER_REVIEW_REQUIRED: true (S4-02 owner checkpoint after fresh review)

## Outcome and authority

From one exact supported candidate generator-support FindingRevision, Site Financials shows a **modelled, assumption-conditioned potential fuel-cost exposure** from zero to a stated upper amount only when a reviewed `fuel-cost-1` quantity bound and a price valid across the whole consequence window exist. Open old and new consequence revisions after a backdated SYSTEM price correction; the FindingRevision and technical quantity remain fixed. Missing price is `UNPRICED` with null amount, unsupported quantity is `QUANTITY_UNAVAILABLE`, and a lagging projection is `STALE/PENDING`, never a zero or old amount presented as current. Authority: `D-2026-10-13-s4-bounded-financial-basis`, `.agent/architect-A-S4-financial-answers.md`, review carries M1/M2/L1/L5/L6, S4-01/S4-03 exact revision and accepted-lineage contracts. Mock `frontend/mockups/v69/index.html#/financials` and `#/assumptions`, manifest `financials:1-3`, `assumptions:1-3`; their prices and F-104 are illustrative.

Built anchors: `backend/assetops_backend/analytics/{dispatch_v3.py,finding_read.py}`, `backend/assetops_backend/finding_api.py`, `backend/assetops_backend/sites/models.py` `specific-fuel-consumption` L/kWh, `backend/assetops_backend/analytics/dispatch.py` legacy `SFC_UNCERTAINTY` (comparison only; do not import `dispatch-2` fuel results), S4-03 Evidence/History route and `frontend/src/sites/{SiteFinding.tsx,findingClient.ts}`. Extend the existing Site root/selection. The technical design's row/DTO sketches at lines 54/165 have one assessment ID, optional one assumption ID and scalar quantity; this decision supersedes that shape for S4-02b: migration and wire must carry explicit bounds, multi-link rows and a separate basis digest.

## Reviewed quantity contract and fixture

1. Version `fuel-cost-1` independently of `dispatch-3.1`. Read one CURRENT exact FindingRevision, its selected primary **and all** supporting AssessmentRevision/analytic-run IDs, accepted public generator-power means, candidate segment `[start,end)` spans, as-accepted Foundation/binding revisions and the physical `specific-fuel-consumption` (L/kWh). Revalidate input membership and coverage from accepted IDs; a Finding's candidate minutes alone is not a fuel quantity. Do not use Lab private truth, legacy `dispatch-2` fuel outputs, a constant inferred load, interpolated missing intervals, or Indeterminate/Necessary spans.
2. `fuel-cost-1` uses the immutable, dimensionless model parameter `sfc_upper_multiplier = 1.10`, ratified as an expressly conditional assumption that actual L/kWh does not exceed 1.10 Ã— the selected Foundation SFC (Architect Q1, `.agent/architect-S4-02-answers.md`; addendum to `D-2026-10-13-s4-bounded-financial-basis`). It is not a calibrated or measured bound and not the legacy `SFC_UNCERTAINTY`. Its version records value, inequality, scope, source, reviewer/date, formula and immutable ID/digest; a later value needs a new version, never an in-place change. **Input rule (Architect C4, fail-closed containment):** `T_i` is the exact `[start,end)` of each stored `CANDIDATE` segment with `observed: true` (there is no `T_i,high`; never use interval `upper_minutes`, `off_before` or `off_after`). Build the union `C` of those spans for the exact FindingRevision, per generator asset. Select the complete accepted, good, nonnegative `GEN_POWER` mean intervals intersecting `C`; each `[a_j,b_j)` must lie wholly inside contiguous Candidate time for that asset, their union must cover `C` without gaps, and same-asset intervals must not overlap (refuse duplicates/conflicts). Each interval needs one unambiguous positive time-valid SFC throughout. Any failure for any span makes the **whole** consequence `QUANTITY_UNAVAILABLE` with no amount. **Formula:** `quantity_low = 0 L`; `quantity_high = 1.10 Ã— Î£_j (P_j,mean kW Ã— (b_j âˆ’ a_j) h Ã— SFC_j L/kWh)`, each distinct interval counted once, unrounded Decimal. Never compute `max(mean) Ã— segment duration` or prorate an interval across a segment cut. Store each counted interval once with power, duration, SFC revision, Candidate spans covered and containment result, plus parameter version/ID and canonical input digest. **Fixtures:** positive complete case; positive case with one interval crossing only the shared edge of two contiguous observed Candidate segments (counted once); open dispatch interval with `upper_minutes = null` but complete contained coverage (quantifiable from stored endpoints). Unavailable: missing power; coverage gap; interval crossing Candidateâ†’Necessary and Candidateâ†’Indeterminate (including where mean Ã— Candidate duration would understate energy); interval into unobserved or outside-Finding time; overlapping/conflicting power; missing, nonpositive, conflicting or mid-interval changing SFC/binding. Unavailable fixtures assert no numeric high or amount; positive fixtures recompute from exact accepted IDs after reload. Default plain wording, final copy at the owner checkpoint: "Modelled potential fuel-cost exposure: 0 to [amount], under the reviewed fuel-cost-1 assumptions. This is not measured fuel saved or a physical maximum." Model name, multiplier, IDs and digest go in details/lineage.
3. Price selection requires one compatible Site `diesel_price_per_litre` revision valid for the **entire** consequence window and known at selected recorded cutoff. The consequence window is the FindingRevision `window_start/end`. A price boundary inside that window leaves it unpriced (`PRICE_SPANS_WINDOW`); do not silently partition quantities or use current price for old operation. Unit/currency mismatch, missing/overlapping/conflicting price or Foundation basis yields typed unavailable/unpriced reason, not a guessed amount. A future-effective price leaves yesterday's selected price and consequence current. A backdated correction valid over yesterday's whole window appends a new consequence for the same FindingRevision and quantity/basis. For a partial-window correction, change only consequences whose full-window selected price changes; a correction that makes a previously priced window cross a price boundary appends an `UNPRICED` consequence revision. `STALE/PENDING` compares the price selected **for that consequence window** and the latest selected FindingRevision with the consequence's pinned IDs; supersession of an unrelated future slice alone is not stale.

## Migration, recompute and reads

- New append-only `financial_consequence_revision`: UUID, tenant/Site/Finding/FindingRevision, consequence type `POTENTIAL_FUEL_COST`, revision number, half-open window, overlap group, basis kind `MODELLED_CONDITIONAL`, formula version, quantity low/high/unit, amount low/high/currency nullable, price selection/reason, limitations, created/recorded time, canonical technical-input digest and separate consequence basis digest. FK/unique `(finding_revision_id,consequence_type,revision_no)` and unique idempotent basis digest; indexes for Site/Finding/window. Link tables `financial_consequence_assessment_revision` (primary plus every supporting exact assessment) and `financial_consequence_assumption_revision` (every used exact price/parameter assumption when represented as an assumption); evidence IDs/accepted envelopes resolve through S4-03. Do not mutate any older row or assessment/Finding. A `quantity` reference scalar, if retained for compatibility, is explicitly labelled, never shown as proved saving.
- On assumption publication or changed selected FindingRevision, record transactional dirty/outbox work keyed by affected Site/key/window/selected revision. Recompute transactionally or retry a durable worker; show `STALE/PENDING` while selection has outrun the consequence. Exact retry returns the existing consequence ID; failed retry leaves typed pending/error, not a silent old current amount. A new FindingRevision produces its own linked consequence. Keep old `UNPRICED`/priced revisions inspectable by ID.
- Multiply unrounded compatible Decimal liters Ã— currency/L to store unrounded low/high. Display low rounded downward and high upward to that currency's minor unit (including non-2-decimal currencies); preserve unrounded values for any later permitted total. Never sum unlike currency, period, basis, overlap group, FindingRevision, scenario or operational lines. Expose selected amount and explicit exclusions; no portfolio total.
- `GET /api/sites/{site_code}/findings/{finding_id}/financial-consequences?revision_id=&consequence_revision_id=&after_revision_no=&limit=` (or equivalent child read) returns exact Finding selection, current/historical consequence selection, complete paged history, price/quantity/amount bounds, valid/recorded times, model/parameter and all assessment/assumption/evidence lineage IDs plus typed `UNPRICED`, `QUANTITY_UNAVAILABLE`, `STALE/PENDING`, closed-source and 401/403/404/503 states. Exact bad/foreign IDs never fall back. Old pinned row is labelled historical; Finding History and S4-03 Evidence links preserve the same revision. The Assumptions History view shows exact price revisions and consequence revisions; the current view never silently substitutes a pinned old price.

## Reviewed quantity contract and fixture

1. Version `fuel-cost-1` independently of `dispatch-3.1`. Do not use Lab private truth, legacy `dispatch-2` fuel outputs, a constant inferred load, interpolated missing intervals, or Indeterminate/Necessary spans.
2. `fuel-cost-1` uses the immutable, dimensionless model parameter `sfc_upper_multiplier = 1.10`, ratified as an expressly conditional assumption that actual L/kWh does not exceed 1.10 Ã— the selected Foundation SFC (Architect Q1, `.agent/architect-S4-02-answers.md`; addendum to `D-2026-10-13-s4-bounded-financial-basis`). It is not a calibrated or measured bound and not the legacy `SFC_UNCERTAINTY`. Its version records value, inequality, scope, source, reviewer/date, formula and immutable ID/digest; a later value needs a new version, never an in-place change. **Input rule (Architect C4, fail-closed containment):** `T_i` is the exact `[start,end)` of each stored `CANDIDATE` segment with `observed: true` (there is no `T_i,high`; never use interval `upper_minutes`, `off_before` or `off_after`). Build the union `C` of those spans for the exact FindingRevision, per generator asset. Select the complete accepted, good, nonnegative `GEN_POWER` mean intervals intersecting `C`; each `[a_j,b_j)` must lie wholly inside contiguous Candidate time for that asset, their union must cover `C` without gaps, and same-asset intervals must not overlap (refuse duplicates/conflicts). Each interval needs one unambiguous positive time-valid SFC throughout. Any failure for any span makes the **whole** consequence `QUANTITY_UNAVAILABLE` with no amount. **Formula:** `quantity_low = 0 L`; `quantity_high = 1.10 Ã— Î£_j (P_j,mean kW Ã— (b_j âˆ’ a_j) h Ã— SFC_j L/kWh)`, each distinct interval counted once, unrounded Decimal. Never compute `max(mean) Ã— segment duration` or prorate an interval across a segment cut. Store each counted interval once with power, duration, SFC revision, Candidate spans covered and containment result, plus parameter version/ID and canonical input digest. **Fixtures:** positive complete case; positive case with one interval crossing only the shared edge of two contiguous observed Candidate segments (counted once); open dispatch interval with `upper_minutes = null` but complete contained coverage (quantifiable from stored endpoints). Unavailable: missing power; coverage gap; interval crossing Candidateâ†’Necessary and Candidateâ†’Indeterminate (including where mean Ã— Candidate duration would understate energy); interval into unobserved or outside-Finding time; overlapping/conflicting power; missing, nonpositive, conflicting or mid-interval changing SFC/binding. Unavailable fixtures assert no numeric high or amount; positive fixtures recompute from exact accepted IDs after reload. Default plain wording, final copy at the owner checkpoint: "Modelled potential fuel-cost exposure: 0 to [amount], under the reviewed fuel-cost-1 assumptions. This is not measured fuel saved or a physical maximum." Model name, multiplier, IDs and digest go in details/lineage.
3. Price selection requires one compatible Site `diesel_price_per_litre` revision valid for the **entire** consequence window and known at selected recorded cutoff. The consequence window is the FindingRevision `window_start/end`. A price boundary inside that window leaves it unpriced (`PRICE_SPANS_WINDOW`); do not silently partition quantities or use current price for old operation. Unit/currency mismatch, missing/overlapping/conflicting price or Foundation basis yields typed unavailable/unpriced reason, not a guessed amount. A future-effective price leaves yesterday's selected price and consequence current. A backdated correction valid over yesterday's whole window appends a new consequence for the same FindingRevision and quantity/basis. For a partial-window correction, change only consequences whose full-window selected price changes; a correction that makes a previously priced window cross a price boundary appends an `UNPRICED` consequence revision. `STALE/PENDING` compares the price selected **for that consequence window** and the latest selected FindingRevision with the consequence's pinned IDs; supersession of an unrelated future slice alone is not stale.

  affected valid range. `financial_consequence_work_attempt` records each recompute attempt (phase 2a worker);
  work without a SUCCEEDED attempt is pending. FindingRevisions that predate this migration are enqueued once
  by the upgrade itself (review L4), so no Finding is left with neither a consequence nor pending work.

-- A consequence names its own FindingRevision's Finding and window, and extends its chain by exactly one.
CREATE FUNCTION financial_consequence_revision_lineage() RETURNS trigger
LANGUAGE plpgsql AS $$
DECLARE
    fr finding_revision%ROWTYPE;
    prior financial_consequence_revision%ROWTYPE;
    latest integer;
BEGIN
    SELECT * INTO fr FROM finding_revision
        WHERE tenant_id = NEW.tenant_id AND site_id = NEW.site_id AND id = NEW.finding_revision_id;
    IF fr.finding_id IS DISTINCT FROM NEW.finding_id THEN
        RAISE EXCEPTION 'financial_consequence_revision names a FindingRevision of another Finding';
    END IF;
    IF fr.episode_start IS DISTINCT FROM NEW.window_start OR fr.episode_end IS DISTINCT FROM NEW.window_end THEN
        RAISE EXCEPTION 'financial_consequence_revision window is not its FindingRevision window';
    END IF;
    -- Review L6: a priced row's value and currency are its price revision's own.
    IF NEW.price_revision_id IS NOT NULL AND NOT EXISTS (
        SELECT 1 FROM financial_assumption_revision p WHERE p.tenant_id = NEW.tenant_id AND p.site_id = NEW.site_id
          AND p.id = NEW.price_revision_id AND p.assumption_key = 'diesel_price_per_litre'
          AND p.value = NEW.price_value AND p.currency = NEW.price_currency) THEN
        RAISE EXCEPTION 'financial_consequence_revision price is not its price revision''s value and currency';
    END IF;
    SELECT max(revision_no) INTO latest FROM financial_consequence_revision
        WHERE finding_revision_id = NEW.finding_revision_id AND consequence_type = NEW.consequence_type;
    IF NEW.revision_no <> coalesce(latest, 0) + 1 THEN
        RAISE EXCEPTION 'financial_consequence_revision revision_no must extend its chain by one';
    END IF;
    IF NEW.prior_consequence_revision_id IS NOT NULL THEN
        SELECT * INTO prior FROM financial_consequence_revision WHERE id = NEW.prior_consequence_revision_id;
        IF prior.finding_revision_id IS DISTINCT FROM NEW.finding_revision_id
           OR prior.consequence_type IS DISTINCT FROM NEW.consequence_type
           OR prior.revision_no IS DISTINCT FROM NEW.revision_no - 1 THEN
            RAISE EXCEPTION 'financial_consequence_revision prior is not the previous revision of its chain';
        END IF;
    END IF;
    RETURN NEW;
END;
$$;
CREATE TRIGGER financial_consequence_revision_lineage BEFORE INSERT ON financial_consequence_revision
    FOR EACH ROW EXECUTE FUNCTION financial_consequence_revision_lineage();

-- Review L6, at commit: a priced row has its PRICE link, and the assessment links are exactly the
-- FindingRevision's INTERVAL assessments.
CREATE FUNCTION financial_consequence_links_complete() RETURNS trigger
LANGUAGE plpgsql AS $$
BEGIN
    IF NEW.state = 'PRICED' AND NOT EXISTS (
        SELECT 1 FROM financial_consequence_assumption_revision l WHERE l.consequence_revision_id = NEW.id
          AND l.assumption_revision_id = NEW.price_revision_id AND l.role = 'PRICE') THEN
        RAISE EXCEPTION 'financial_consequence_revision is PRICED without its PRICE link';
    END IF;
    IF EXISTS (
        (SELECT a.assessment_revision_id, a.analytic_run_id, a.is_primary FROM finding_revision_assessment a
          WHERE a.finding_revision_id = NEW.finding_revision_id AND a.scope = 'INTERVAL'
         EXCEPT SELECT l.assessment_revision_id, l.analytic_run_id, l.is_primary
          FROM financial_consequence_assessment_revision l WHERE l.consequence_revision_id = NEW.id)) THEN
        RAISE EXCEPTION 'financial_consequence_revision does not link every INTERVAL assessment of its FindingRevision';
    END IF;
    RETURN NULL;
END;
$$;
CREATE CONSTRAINT TRIGGER financial_consequence_links_complete AFTER INSERT ON financial_consequence_revision
    DEFERRABLE INITIALLY DEFERRED FOR EACH ROW EXECUTE FUNCTION financial_consequence_links_complete();

-- A consequence may cite only assessments its FindingRevision itself links.
CREATE FUNCTION financial_consequence_assessment_linked() RETURNS trigger
LANGUAGE plpgsql AS $$
BEGIN
    IF NOT EXISTS (
        SELECT 1 FROM financial_consequence_revision c
        JOIN finding_revision_assessment a ON a.finding_revision_id = c.finding_revision_id
        WHERE c.id = NEW.consequence_revision_id AND a.assessment_revision_id = NEW.assessment_revision_id
          AND a.analytic_run_id = NEW.analytic_run_id AND a.scope = 'INTERVAL' AND a.is_primary = NEW.is_primary) THEN
        RAISE EXCEPTION 'financial_consequence_assessment_revision is not an INTERVAL assessment of its FindingRevision';
    END IF;
    RETURN NEW;
END;
$$;
CREATE TRIGGER financial_consequence_assessment_linked BEFORE INSERT ON financial_consequence_assessment_revision
    FOR EACH ROW EXECUTE FUNCTION financial_consequence_assessment_linked();

-- Transactional dirty work: an assumption publication dirties its affected valid range (a SUCCESSION also
-- changes everything after its start, because it closes the prior open-ended assignment there).
CREATE FUNCTION financial_consequence_dirty_on_assumption() RETURNS trigger
LANGUAGE plpgsql AS $$
BEGIN
    INSERT INTO financial_consequence_work (tenant_id, site_id, cause, assumption_key, assumption_revision_id,
                                            affected_from, affected_to)
    VALUES (NEW.tenant_id, NEW.site_id, 'ASSUMPTION_PUBLISHED', NEW.assumption_key, NEW.id, NEW.valid_from,
            CASE WHEN NEW.change_kind = 'SUCCESSION' THEN NULL ELSE NEW.valid_to END)
    ON CONFLICT (assumption_revision_id) DO NOTHING;
    RETURN NULL;
END;
$$;
CREATE TRIGGER financial_consequence_dirty_on_assumption AFTER INSERT ON financial_assumption_revision
    FOR EACH ROW EXECUTE FUNCTION financial_consequence_dirty_on_assumption();

CREATE FUNCTION financial_consequence_dirty_on_finding_revision() RETURNS trigger
LANGUAGE plpgsql AS $$
BEGIN
    INSERT INTO financial_consequence_work (tenant_id, site_id, cause, finding_id, finding_revision_id,
                                            affected_from, affected_to)
    VALUES (NEW.tenant_id, NEW.site_id, 'FINDING_REVISION_APPENDED', NEW.finding_id, NEW.id, NEW.episode_start,
            NEW.episode_end)
    ON CONFLICT (finding_revision_id) DO NOTHING;
    RETURN NULL;
END;
$$;
CREATE TRIGGER financial_consequence_dirty_on_finding_revision AFTER INSERT ON finding_revision
    FOR EACH ROW EXECUTE FUNCTION financial_consequence_dirty_on_finding_revision();

-- Review L4 (bootstrap): FindingRevisions recorded before this migration get the same work row the trigger
-- would have written, so the recompute worker derives their consequences with the current price.
INSERT INTO financial_consequence_work (tenant_id, site_id, cause, finding_id, finding_revision_id, affected_from,
                                        affected_to)
SELECT tenant_id, site_id, 'FINDING_REVISION_APPENDED', finding_id, id, episode_start, episode_end
FROM finding_revision ORDER BY created_at, id;
"""

"""Durable `fuel-cost-1` consequence recompute (S4-02b phase 2a).

Packet `tasks/S4-02b-fuel-consequence.md` "Migration, recompute and reads": dirty work rows are written by
migration 0011's triggers in the assumption-publication or FindingRevision transaction (and once for every
FindingRevision that predates 0011). This worker drains them:

    pending_work -> load_input -> quantify -> select_window_price -> consequence -> append -> record_attempt

- `FINDING_REVISION_APPENDED` recomputes that exact FindingRevision (a new FindingRevision gets its own
  consequence chain, even when a later revision has since superseded it).
- `ASSUMPTION_PUBLISHED` recomputes the latest revision of every Finding whose episode overlaps the
  publication's affected valid range `[affected_from, affected_to)`.

Each target is derived from the exact persisted inputs and the price timeline known now, and appended
idempotently: an unchanged basis replays the stored ID (review M1 keeps an unrelated publication from
re-revising), a changed one appends revision n+1. A failure records a typed FAILED attempt and leaves the work
pending, so the read shows STALE/PENDING rather than an old amount as current; the next run retries. A crash
between `append` and `record_attempt` is safe: the retry replays the same consequence ID.

This module does no I/O of its own; stores are injected (composition builds them).
"""

from __future__ import annotations

from dataclasses import dataclass, field
from typing import Any, Protocol
from uuid import UUID

from assetops_backend.financials import fuel_cost as fc

ERROR_STORE_UNAVAILABLE = "STORE_UNAVAILABLE"
ERROR_FINDING_REVISION_NOT_FOUND = "FINDING_REVISION_NOT_FOUND"
ERROR_RECOMPUTE_FAILED = "RECOMPUTE_FAILED"


class ConsequenceStore(Protocol):
    def load_input(self, tenant_id: UUID, site_id: UUID, finding_id: UUID,
                   finding_revision_id: UUID) -> fc.FindingInput | None: ...

    def append(self, c_: fc.Consequence) -> Any: ...

    def pending_work(self, tenant_id: UUID, site_id: UUID) -> list[dict[str, Any]]: ...

    def record_attempt(self, tenant_id: UUID, site_id: UUID, work_id: UUID, **kw: Any) -> int: ...

    def latest_revisions_overlapping(self, tenant_id: UUID, site_id: UUID, lo: Any,
                                     hi: Any) -> list[tuple[UUID, UUID]]: ...


class PriceStore(Protocol):
    def snapshot(self, tenant_id: UUID, site_id: UUID, key: str, recorded_at: Any, after_revision_no: int,
                 limit: int) -> dict[str, Any]: ...


class FindingRevisionMissing(LookupError):
    pass


def window_price(prices: PriceStore, tenant_id: UUID, site_id: UUID, f: fc.FindingInput) -> fc.PriceSelection:
    """The whole-window price selection from the current price timeline (recorded cutoff: now)."""
    snap = prices.snapshot(tenant_id, site_id, fc.PRICE_KEY, None, 0, 1)
    return fc.select_window_price(snap["timeline"], snap["cited"], f.window_start, f.window_end)


def derive(store: ConsequenceStore, prices: PriceStore, tenant_id: UUID, site_id: UUID, finding_id: UUID,
           finding_revision_id: UUID) -> fc.Consequence:
    """The consequence the exact persisted inputs and today's price timeline give, not yet stored."""
    f = store.load_input(tenant_id, site_id, finding_id, finding_revision_id)
    if f is None:
        raise FindingRevisionMissing(f"FindingRevision {finding_revision_id} is not this Site's Finding's.")
    q = fc.quantify(f)
    price = fc.NOT_EVALUATED if q.state != "AVAILABLE" else window_price(prices, tenant_id, site_id, f)
    return fc.consequence(f, q, price)


@dataclass
class WorkOutcome:
    work_id: UUID
    cause: str
    succeeded: bool
    attempt_no: int
    consequence_revision_ids: list[UUID] = field(default_factory=list)
    appended: list[UUID] = field(default_factory=list)
    replayed: list[UUID] = field(default_factory=list)
    error_code: str | None = None
    error_detail: str | None = None


class ConsequenceRecomputeWorker:
    def __init__(self, store: ConsequenceStore, prices: PriceStore,
                 unavailable: tuple[type[BaseException], ...] = ()) -> None:
        self._store = store
        self._prices = prices
        self._unavailable = unavailable

    def targets(self, tenant_id: UUID, site_id: UUID, work: dict[str, Any]) -> list[tuple[UUID, UUID]]:
        if work["cause"] == "FINDING_REVISION_APPENDED":
            return [(work["finding_id"], work["finding_revision_id"])]
        return self._store.latest_revisions_overlapping(tenant_id, site_id, work["affected_from"],
                                                        work["affected_to"])

    def process(self, tenant_id: UUID, site_id: UUID, work: dict[str, Any]) -> WorkOutcome:
        out = WorkOutcome(work["id"], work["cause"], False, 0)
        try:
            for finding_id, revision_id in self.targets(tenant_id, site_id, work):
                appended = self._store.append(derive(self._store, self._prices, tenant_id, site_id, finding_id,
                                                     revision_id))
                out.consequence_revision_ids.append(appended.consequence_revision_id)
                (out.replayed if appended.replayed else out.appended).append(appended.consequence_revision_id)
        except FindingRevisionMissing as error:
            out.error_code, out.error_detail = ERROR_FINDING_REVISION_NOT_FOUND, str(error)
        except self._unavailable as error:
            out.error_code, out.error_detail = ERROR_STORE_UNAVAILABLE, str(error)
        except Exception as error:  # noqa: BLE001 - any failure is recorded as typed pending work, never lost
            out.error_code, out.error_detail = ERROR_RECOMPUTE_FAILED, f"{type(error).__name__}: {error}"
        if out.error_code is None:
            out.succeeded = True
            out.attempt_no = self._store.record_attempt(
                tenant_id, site_id, work["id"], succeeded=True,
                consequence_revision_ids=tuple(out.consequence_revision_ids), skip_if_succeeded=True)
        else:
            out.attempt_no = self._store.record_attempt(
                tenant_id, site_id, work["id"], succeeded=False, error_code=out.error_code,
                error_detail=out.error_detail[:2000] if out.error_detail else None)
        return out

    def run_pending(self, tenant_id: UUID, site_id: UUID, limit: int | None = None) -> list[WorkOutcome]:
        """Drain this Site's pending work oldest first; failed items stay pending for the next run."""
        pending = self._store.pending_work(tenant_id, site_id)
        return [self.process(tenant_id, site_id, w) for w in pending[:limit]]

    def latest_revisions_overlapping(self, tenant_id: UUID, site_id: UUID, lo: datetime,
                                     hi: datetime | None) -> list[tuple[UUID, UUID]]:
        """(finding_id, latest FindingRevision id) of every Finding of this Site whose latest revision's
        episode overlaps `[lo, hi)` (half-open; `hi` None is open-ended)."""
        def work(c: Connection):
            return [(r[0], r[1]) for r in c.execute(text(
                "SELECT r.finding_id, r.id FROM finding_revision r WHERE r.tenant_id = :t AND r.site_id = :s "
                "AND r.revision_no = (SELECT max(x.revision_no) FROM finding_revision x WHERE x.finding_id = "
                "r.finding_id) AND r.episode_end > :lo "
                "AND (CAST(:hi AS timestamptz) IS NULL OR r.episode_start < CAST(:hi AS timestamptz)) "
                "ORDER BY r.episode_start, r.id"), {"t": tenant_id, "s": site_id, "lo": lo, "hi": hi})]
        return self._run(work, "REPEATABLE READ")

    def locate(self, tenant_id: UUID, site_id: UUID, finding_id: UUID,
               consequence_revision_id: UUID) -> UUID | None:
        """The FindingRevision of one exact consequence revision of this Site's Finding, else None."""
        def work(c: Connection):
            return c.execute(text(
                "SELECT finding_revision_id FROM financial_consequence_revision WHERE tenant_id = :t "
                "AND site_id = :s AND finding_id = :f AND id = :c"),
                {"t": tenant_id, "s": site_id, "f": finding_id, "c": consequence_revision_id}).scalar_one_or_none()
        return self._run(work)

    def chain(self, tenant_id: UUID, site_id: UUID, finding_id: UUID, finding_revision_id: UUID, *,
              consequence_revision_id: UUID | None, after_revision_no: int, limit: int) -> dict[str, Any]:

        keyset page, the lineage links of every returned revision and the pending work that touches it."""

+# S4-02c — consequence work on accepted evidence
+
+Status: implementation-ready
+USER_REVIEW_REQUIRED: false (no new UI or owner-facing copy; independent implementation review required)
+Milestone: S4 Finding + Financials
+Depends on: merged S2-02 and reviewed/merged S4-01, S4-03, S4-02a/b; resolved `A-S4-financial` and `A-S5-overview`. S5-01's current money read depends on this packet's reviewed result.
+Branch when activated: `task/S4-02c-evidence-consequence-work`
+Planner: Codex, 2026-10-14
+
+## Outcome and authority
+
+An accepted late generator-power mean that can alter an existing Site FindingRevision's `fuel-cost-1` input creates durable consequence work in the same database transaction as acceptance. The Site read shows the old consequence as `STALE` (or `PENDING` if no consequence exists) with real queued work, then a scheduled, retryable worker derives and appends the new exact-basis consequence. The S5-01 selected-window read may use money only after that consequence is `CURRENT` and `PRICED` for its selected FindingRevision and window. A fresh stale read alone does not complete this slice.
+
+Authority: `D-2026-10-13-s4-bounded-financial-basis`, `D-2026-10-14-s402-post-review-follow-ons`, `D-2026-10-14-s5-selected-window-overview`, `.agent/architect-S4-02-batch-answers.md` Q2 and `.agent/architect-contest-2026-10-14d-answers.md` (Planner refinement). This is registry node `I-evidence-acceptance-consequence-work`, separate from S4-02a/b and S5-01's UI checkpoint.
+
+Built anchors: `.ai/CODE_STATE.md` S2-02 and S4-02b phases 1/2a/2b; `backend/assetops_backend/evidence/adapters/postgres_evidence_ledger.py` (`process_batch`/`_persist`, accepted evidence and disposition in one transaction), `backend/migrations/versions/0011_financial_consequences.py` (work, attempts and existing triggers), `backend/assetops_backend/financials/{recompute.py,consequence_read.py,adapters/postgres_consequence_store.py}`, and `backend/assetops_backend/recompute_consequences.py`. Reuse `tools/s402b_power_cases.py` and `tools/s402b_fuel_cost_walkthrough.py` as isolated fixture/walkthrough bases. The S4-02b read already detects `TECHNICAL_INPUT_CHANGED` for an unchanged FindingRevision, but acceptance currently enqueues no consequence work; its one-shot CLI has no run schedule.
+
+## Acceptance, work and worker contract
+
+1. Add a migration to extend `financial_consequence_work` with an `EVIDENCE_ACCEPTED` cause and a tenant/Site-scoped FK to the exact `accepted_evidence.id`. Keep existing assumption and FindingRevision causes and rows valid. Each new row identifies the accepted evidence, target Finding and latest eligible FindingRevision at enqueue time, and its half-open affected interval. Constrain cause shape, range, scope and a unique `(accepted_evidence_id, finding_revision_id, cause)` key; duplicates and conflicting evidence create no second row. Index pending selection by Site and due time. Preserve append-only evidence, work and attempt history. Migration upgrade/downgrade and pre-existing rows must be proved.
+2. In the S2-02 acceptance transaction, after a genuinely new accepted evidence ID is returned, select potentially affected existing Site Findings by coarse half-open interval overlap with the accepted interval and the generator-power role. Insert scoped work before commit. If the insert fails, acceptance and its disposition roll back; it must never leave a committed accepted reading with a lost required work row. Exact replay, duplicate, conflict and rejected decisions do not enqueue. If the transaction contains several accepted intervals, each exact accepted ID is deduplicated against its target. Do not trigger on a client-declared role or from a later read. Broad selection may queue a candidate that later no-ops, but must not omit a possibly affected Finding. FindingRevision insertion retains migration 0011's own trigger so findings first created after acceptance also get work.
+3. The worker treats the queued revision as a locator, then rechecks tenant/Site, accepted disposition, bound role/asset, half-open interval overlap, candidate episode/window and the **latest eligible FindingRevision** for that Finding at processing time. Derive against that exact current revision and its accepted public inputs only. A superseded or irrelevant target records a successful typed no-op; if a newer eligible revision exists, process that revision once (its insertion trigger may also queue it). No-op on unrelated roles/assets/windows without appending a consequence. A missing or closed source stays typed and retryable when transient; wrong-Site scope never falls back. Price and technical basis selection remain the reviewed S4-02b contract; no extra amount or quantity shortcut is introduced. The existing unique consequence basis and append lock must make unchanged or repeated work return the existing ID, including concurrent workers and an append-then-crash retry.
+4. Make the run plan operational: extend the server-side CLI to drain a configured tenant/Site (or a scoped active-Site iterator) on a documented one-minute recurring service/timer, with bounded batch size, a database claim/lease or equivalent single-consumer lock, persisted retry eligibility/backoff, and a restart-safe failure record. A failed item remains visible but cannot hot-loop inside one run; a later scheduled run retries it. Print/record selected, appended, replayed, no-op, failed and backlog counts with Site scope; document deployment invocation, ownership, cadence and recovery. The scheduler must not rely on a user opening Financials. Existing price/Finding work uses the same runner. A work item becomes succeeded only after all its selected targets have safely appended/replayed or no-opped; crash and concurrent-run tests must prove eventual drain without duplicate consequence basis.
+5. Keep the consequence read's `CURRENT`/`STALE`/`PENDING`/`HISTORICAL` and typed reasons. Show queued/pending status only when a real unsucceeded work row touches the selected revision; if currentness is stale but no work exists, report that discrepancy explicitly and do not claim queued. S5-01 uses only a `CURRENT`/`PRICED`, same Site/window/FindingRevision/basis consequence after work finishes. No new UI copy or mock panel is authorized here; a necessary owner-facing copy change reopens `USER_REVIEW_REQUIRED` and its checkpoint.
+
+## Phases and focused proof
+
+Each phase fits one Claude Implementer context below approximately 120k tokens and receives an independent fresh review before the next.
+
+| Phase | Reviewable result and focused proof |
+| --- | --- |
+| 1. Transactional acceptance work | Migration, scoped accepted-evidence FK/uniqueness, acceptance integration. Postgres tests prove committed accepted late power plus one work row, rollback atomicity, exact retry/duplicate/conflict/rejection, unrelated Site and zero-overlap, half-open edge, and existing migration 0011 causes/backfill. |
+| 2. Scoped drain and run plan | Role/asset/window/latest-revision recheck, typed no-op, idempotent append, claim/retry/backoff and recurring runner instructions. Test irrelevant accepted input, revised Finding between enqueue and drain, wrong Site, two workers, failure then scheduled retry, append-then-crash, restart and bounded batch; inspect exact work/attempt/consequence IDs and no duplicate basis. |
+| 3. Late-power end-to-end walkthrough | On an isolated Postgres copy of the S4-02b power fixture, first persist an exact FindingRevision and consequence, then accept a **late** good generator-power interval that changes its technical digest without relying on a new FindingRevision. Before the scheduled drain, assert `STALE/TECHNICAL_INPUT_CHANGED` and the queued work ID (or `PENDING` with work when no head); after drain, assert new consequence revision, changed accepted-evidence/technical digest, same or explicitly superseded eligible FindingRevision, old version retained, current priced eligibility for S5-01, and reload stability. Include an unrelated accepted reading that succeeds as no-op. Record commands and IDs, not illustrative mock money. |

+## Outcome and authority
+
+An accepted late generator-power mean that can alter an existing Site FindingRevision's `fuel-cost-1` input creates durable consequence work in the same database transaction as acceptance. The Site read shows the old consequence as `STALE` (or `PENDING` if no consequence exists) with real queued work, then a scheduled, retryable worker derives and appends the new exact-basis consequence. The S5-01 selected-window read may use money only after that consequence is `CURRENT` and `PRICED` for its selected FindingRevision and window. A fresh stale read alone does not complete this slice.
+
+Authority: `D-2026-10-13-s4-bounded-financial-basis`, `D-2026-10-14-s402-post-review-follow-ons`, `D-2026-10-14-s5-selected-window-overview`, `.agent/architect-S4-02-batch-answers.md` Q2 and `.agent/architect-contest-2026-10-14d-answers.md` (Planner refinement). Reuse `tools/s402b_power_cases.py` and `tools/s402b_fuel_cost_walkthrough.py` as isolated fixture/walkthrough bases. The S4-02b read already detects `TECHNICAL_INPUT_CHANGED` for an unchanged FindingRevision, but acceptance currently enqueues no consequence work; its one-shot CLI has no run schedule.

+## Acceptance, work and worker contract
+
+1. Add a migration to extend `financial_consequence_work` with an `EVIDENCE_ACCEPTED` cause and a tenant/Site-scoped FK to the exact `accepted_evidence.id`. Keep existing assumption and FindingRevision causes and rows valid. Each new row identifies the accepted evidence, target Finding and latest eligible FindingRevision at enqueue time, and its half-open affected interval. Constrain cause shape, range, scope and a unique `(accepted_evidence_id, finding_revision_id, cause)` key; duplicates and conflicting evidence create no second row. Index pending selection by Site and due time. Preserve append-only evidence, work and attempt history. Migration upgrade/downgrade and pre-existing rows must be proved.
+2. In the S2-02 acceptance transaction, after a genuinely new accepted evidence ID is returned, select potentially affected existing Site Findings by coarse half-open interval overlap with the accepted interval and the generator-power role. Insert scoped work before commit. If the insert fails, acceptance and its disposition roll back; it must never leave a committed accepted reading with a lost required work row. Exact replay, duplicate, conflict and rejected decisions do not enqueue. If the transaction contains several accepted intervals, each exact accepted ID is deduplicated against its target. Do not trigger on a client-declared role or from a later read. Broad selection may queue a candidate that later no-ops, but must not omit a possibly affected Finding. FindingRevision insertion retains migration 0011's own trigger so findings first created after acceptance also get work.
+3. The worker treats the queued revision as a locator, then rechecks tenant/Site, accepted disposition, bound role/asset, half-open interval overlap, candidate episode/window and the **latest eligible FindingRevision** for that Finding at processing time. Derive against that exact current revision and its accepted public inputs only. A superseded or irrelevant target records a successful typed no-op; if a newer eligible revision exists, process that revision once (its insertion trigger may also queue it). No-op on unrelated roles/assets/windows without appending a consequence. A missing or closed source stays typed and retryable when transient; wrong-Site scope never falls back. Price and technical basis selection remain the reviewed S4-02b contract; no extra amount or quantity shortcut is introduced. The existing unique consequence basis and append lock must make unchanged or repeated work return the existing ID, including concurrent workers and an append-then-crash retry.
+4. Make the run plan operational: extend the server-side CLI to drain a configured tenant/Site (or a scoped active-Site iterator) on a documented one-minute recurring service/timer, with bounded batch size, a database claim/lease or equivalent single-consumer lock, persisted retry eligibility/backoff, and a restart-safe failure record. A failed item remains visible but cannot hot-loop inside one run; a later scheduled run retries it. Print/record selected, appended, replayed, no-op, failed and backlog counts with Site scope; document deployment invocation, ownership, cadence and recovery. The scheduler must not rely on a user opening Financials. Existing price/Finding work uses the same runner. A work item becomes succeeded only after all its selected targets have safely appended/replayed or no-opped; crash and concurrent-run tests must prove eventual drain without duplicate consequence basis.
+5. Keep the consequence read's `CURRENT`/`STALE`/`PENDING`/`HISTORICAL` and typed reasons. Show queued/pending status only when a real unsucceeded work row touches the selected revision; if currentness is stale but no work exists, report that discrepancy explicitly and do not claim queued. S5-01 uses only a `CURRENT`/`PRICED`, same Site/window/FindingRevision/basis consequence after work finishes. No new UI copy or mock panel is authorized here; a necessary owner-facing copy change reopens `USER_REVIEW_REQUIRED` and its checkpoint.

+# S4-02c — consequence work on accepted evidence
+
+Status: implementation-ready
+USER_REVIEW_REQUIRED: false (no new UI or owner-facing copy; independent implementation review required)
+Milestone: S4 Finding + Financials
+Depends on: merged S2-02 and reviewed/merged S4-01, S4-03, S4-02a/b; resolved `A-S4-financial` and `A-S5-overview`. S5-01's current money read depends on this packet's reviewed result.
+Branch when activated: `task/S4-02c-evidence-consequence-work`
+Planner: Codex, 2026-10-14
+
+## Outcome and authority
+
+An accepted late generator-power mean that can alter an existing Site FindingRevision's `fuel-cost-1` input creates durable consequence work in the same database transaction as acceptance. The Site read shows the old consequence as `STALE` (or `PENDING` if no consequence exists) with real queued work, then a scheduled, retryable worker derives and appends the new exact-basis consequence. The S5-01 selected-window read may use money only after that consequence is `CURRENT` and `PRICED` for its selected FindingRevision and window. A fresh stale read alone does not complete this slice.
+
+Authority: `D-2026-10-13-s4-bounded-financial-basis`, `D-2026-10-14-s402-post-review-follow-ons`, `D-2026-10-14-s5-selected-window-overview`, `.agent/architect-S4-02-batch-answers.md` Q2 and `.agent/architect-contest-2026-10-14d-answers.md` (Planner refinement). This is registry node `I-evidence-acceptance-consequence-work`, separate from S4-02a/b and S5-01's UI checkpoint.
+
+Built anchors: `.ai/CODE_STATE.md` S2-02 and S4-02b phases 1/2a/2b; `backend/assetops_backend/evidence/adapters/postgres_evidence_ledger.py` (`process_batch`/`_persist`, accepted evidence and disposition in one transaction), `backend/migrations/versions/0011_financial_consequences.py` (work, attempts and existing triggers), `backend/assetops_backend/financials/{recompute.py,consequence_read.py,adapters/postgres_consequence_store.py}`, and `backend/assetops_backend/recompute_consequences.py`. Reuse `tools/s402b_power_cases.py` and `tools/s402b_fuel_cost_walkthrough.py` as isolated fixture/walkthrough bases. The S4-02b read already detects `TECHNICAL_INPUT_CHANGED` for an unchanged FindingRevision, but acceptance currently enqueues no consequence work; its one-shot CLI has no run schedule.
+
+## Acceptance, work and worker contract
+
+1. Add a migration to extend `financial_consequence_work` with an `EVIDENCE_ACCEPTED` cause and a tenant/Site-scoped FK to the exact `accepted_evidence.id`. Keep existing assumption and FindingRevision causes and rows valid. Each new row identifies the accepted evidence, target Finding and latest eligible FindingRevision at enqueue time, and its half-open affected interval. Constrain cause shape, range, scope and a unique `(accepted_evidence_id, finding_revision_id, cause)` key; duplicates and conflicting evidence create no second row. Index pending selection by Site and due time. Preserve append-only evidence, work and attempt history. Migration upgrade/downgrade and pre-existing rows must be proved.
+2. In the S2-02 acceptance transaction, after a genuinely new accepted evidence ID is returned, select potentially affected existing Site Findings by coarse half-open interval overlap with the accepted interval and the generator-power role. Insert scoped work before commit. If the insert fails, acceptance and its disposition roll back; it must never leave a committed accepted reading with a lost required work row. Exact replay, duplicate, conflict and rejected decisions do not enqueue. If the transaction contains several accepted intervals, each exact accepted ID is deduplicated against its target. Do not trigger on a client-declared role or from a later read. Broad selection may queue a candidate that later no-ops, but must not omit a possibly affected Finding. FindingRevision insertion retains migration 0011's own trigger so findings first created after acceptance also get work.
+3. The worker treats the queued revision as a locator, then rechecks tenant/Site, accepted disposition, bound role/asset, half-open interval overlap, candidate episode/window and the **latest eligible FindingRevision** for that Finding at processing time. Derive against that exact current revision and its accepted public inputs only. A superseded or irrelevant target records a successful typed no-op; if a newer eligible revision exists, process that revision once (its insertion trigger may also queue it). No-op on unrelated roles/assets/windows without appending a consequence. A missing or closed source stays typed and retryable when transient; wrong-Site scope never falls back. Price and technical basis selection remain the reviewed S4-02b contract; no extra amount or quantity shortcut is introduced. The existing unique consequence basis and append lock must make unchanged or repeated work return the existing ID, including concurrent workers and an append-then-crash retry.
+4. Make the run plan operational: extend the server-side CLI to drain a configured tenant/Site (or a scoped active-Site iterator) on a documented one-minute recurring service/timer, with bounded batch size, a database claim/lease or equivalent single-consumer lock, persisted retry eligibility/backoff, and a restart-safe failure record. A failed item remains visible but cannot hot-loop inside one run; a later scheduled run retries it. Print/record selected, appended, replayed, no-op, failed and backlog counts with Site scope; document deployment invocation, ownership, cadence and recovery. The scheduler must not rely on a user opening Financials. Existing price/Finding work uses the same runner. A work item becomes succeeded only after all its selected targets have safely appended/replayed or no-opped; crash and concurrent-run tests must prove eventual drain without duplicate consequence basis.
+5. Keep the consequence read's `CURRENT`/`STALE`/`PENDING`/`HISTORICAL` and typed reasons. Show queued/pending status only when a real unsucceeded work row touches the selected revision; if currentness is stale but no work exists, report that discrepancy explicitly and do not claim queued. S5-01 uses only a `CURRENT`/`PRICED`, same Site/window/FindingRevision/basis consequence after work finishes. No new UI copy or mock panel is authorized here; a necessary owner-facing copy change reopens `USER_REVIEW_REQUIRED` and its checkpoint.
+
+## Phases and focused proof
+
+Each phase fits one Claude Implementer context below approximately 120k tokens and receives an independent fresh review before the next.
+
+| Phase | Reviewable result and focused proof |
+| --- | --- |
+| 1. Transactional acceptance work | Migration, scoped accepted-evidence FK/uniqueness, acceptance integration. Postgres tests prove committed accepted late power plus one work row, rollback atomicity, exact retry/duplicate/conflict/rejection, unrelated Site and zero-overlap, half-open edge, and existing migration 0011 causes/backfill. |
+| 2. Scoped drain and run plan | Role/asset/window/latest-revision recheck, typed no-op, idempotent append, claim/retry/backoff and recurring runner instructions. Test irrelevant accepted input, revised Finding between enqueue and drain, wrong Site, two workers, failure then scheduled retry, append-then-crash, restart and bounded batch; inspect exact work/attempt/consequence IDs and no duplicate basis. |
+| 3. Late-power end-to-end walkthrough | On an isolated Postgres copy of the S4-02b power fixture, first persist an exact FindingRevision and consequence, then accept a **late** good generator-power interval that changes its technical digest without relying on a new FindingRevision. Before the scheduled drain, assert `STALE/TECHNICAL_INPUT_CHANGED` and the queued work ID (or `PENDING` with work when no head); after drain, assert new consequence revision, changed accepted-evidence/technical digest, same or explicitly superseded eligible FindingRevision, old version retained, current priced eligibility for S5-01, and reload stability. Include an unrelated accepted reading that succeeds as no-op. Record commands and IDs, not illustrative mock money. |
+
+Reviewer checks migration safety, DB transaction rollback, scope/foreign Site refusal, half-open boundaries, accepted evidence identity, coarse-selection completeness, latest eligible revision, public-only lineage, no-op, retry and currentness. Run focused Postgres/API/model tests, the existing S4-02b walkthrough variant and applicable workflow guards; run `tools/check-all.ps1` when dependencies are installed. Review independently before registry resolution. No separate owner visual checkpoint is needed while this remains non-UI; S5-01 retains its own `USER_REVIEW_REQUIRED` checkpoint.
+
+Out of scope: new fuel model or price semantics, altered S4-02b copy/layout, source-authorship provenance (separate `I-stored-demo-provenance`), equal-start price succession, Assumptions Site consequence history, S5 Overview implementation, private simulator truth, and the owner's broader [analysis input data for simulated and real Sites](../.ai/MILESTONE_REVIEW_BACKLOG.md#owner-analysis-input-data-for-simulated-and-real-sites-2026-10-14) backlog item. This packet proves a late accepted input changes a consequence; it does not fix ordinary gateway power cadence or real-Site input readiness.

+# S4-02c — consequence work on accepted evidence
+
+Status: implementation-ready
+USER_REVIEW_REQUIRED: false (no new UI or owner-facing copy; independent implementation review required)
+Milestone: S4 Finding + Financials
+Depends on: merged S2-02 and reviewed/merged S4-01, S4-03, S4-02a/b; resolved `A-S4-financial` and `A-S5-overview`. S5-01's current money read depends on this packet's reviewed result.
+Branch when activated: `task/S4-02c-evidence-consequence-work`
+Planner: Codex, 2026-10-14
+
+## Outcome and authority
+
+An accepted late generator-power mean that can alter an existing Site FindingRevision's `fuel-cost-1` input creates durable consequence work in the same database transaction as acceptance. The Site read shows the old consequence as `STALE` (or `PENDING` if no consequence exists) with real queued work, then a scheduled, retryable worker derives and appends the new exact-basis consequence. The S5-01 selected-window read may use money only after that consequence is `CURRENT` and `PRICED` for its selected FindingRevision and window. A fresh stale read alone does not complete this slice.
+
+Authority: `D-2026-10-13-s4-bounded-financial-basis`, `D-2026-10-14-s402-post-review-follow-ons`, `D-2026-10-14-s5-selected-window-overview`, `.agent/architect-S4-02-batch-answers.md` Q2 and `.agent/architect-contest-2026-10-14d-answers.md` (Planner refinement). This is registry node `I-evidence-acceptance-consequence-work`, separate from S4-02a/b and S5-01's UI checkpoint.
+
+Built anchors: `.ai/CODE_STATE.md` S2-02 and S4-02b phases 1/2a/2b; `backend/assetops_backend/evidence/adapters/postgres_evidence_ledger.py` (`process_batch`/`_persist`, accepted evidence and disposition in one transaction), `backend/migrations/versions/0011_financial_consequences.py` (work, attempts and existing triggers), `backend/assetops_backend/financials/{recompute.py,consequence_read.py,adapters/postgres_consequence_store.py}`, and `backend/assetops_backend/recompute_consequences.py`. Reuse `tools/s402b_power_cases.py` and `tools/s402b_fuel_cost_walkthrough.py` as isolated fixture/walkthrough bases. The S4-02b read already detects `TECHNICAL_INPUT_CHANGED` for an unchanged FindingRevision, but acceptance currently enqueues no consequence work; its one-shot CLI has no run schedule.
+
+## Acceptance, work and worker contract
+
+1. Add a migration to extend `financial_consequence_work` with an `EVIDENCE_ACCEPTED` cause and a tenant/Site-scoped FK to the exact `accepted_evidence.id`. Keep existing assumption and FindingRevision causes and rows valid. Each new row identifies the accepted evidence, target Finding and latest eligible FindingRevision at enqueue time, and its half-open affected interval. Constrain cause shape, range, scope and a unique `(accepted_evidence_id, finding_revision_id, cause)` key; duplicates and conflicting evidence create no second row. Index pending selection by Site and due time. Preserve append-only evidence, work and attempt history. Migration upgrade/downgrade and pre-existing rows must be proved.
+2. In the S2-02 acceptance transaction, after a genuinely new accepted evidence ID is returned, select potentially affected existing Site Findings by coarse half-open interval overlap with the accepted interval and the generator-power role. Insert scoped work before commit. If the insert fails, acceptance and its disposition roll back; it must never leave a committed accepted reading with a lost required work row. Exact replay, duplicate, conflict and rejected decisions do not enqueue. If the transaction contains several accepted intervals, each exact accepted ID is deduplicated against its target. Do not trigger on a client-declared role or from a later read. Broad selection may queue a candidate that later no-ops, but must not omit a possibly affected Finding. FindingRevision insertion retains migration 0011's own trigger so findings first created after acceptance also get work.
+3. The worker treats the queued revision as a locator, then rechecks tenant/Site, accepted disposition, bound role/asset, half-open interval overlap, candidate episode/window and the **latest eligible FindingRevision** for that Finding at processing time. Derive against that exact current revision and its accepted public inputs only. A superseded or irrelevant target records a successful typed no-op; if a newer eligible revision exists, process that revision once (its insertion trigger may also queue it). No-op on unrelated roles/assets/windows without appending a consequence. A missing or closed source stays typed and retryable when transient; wrong-Site scope never falls back. Price and technical basis selection remain the reviewed S4-02b contract; no extra amount or quantity shortcut is introduced. The existing unique consequence basis and append lock must make unchanged or repeated work return the existing ID, including concurrent workers and an append-then-crash retry.
+4. Make the run plan operational: extend the server-side CLI to drain a configured tenant/Site (or a scoped active-Site iterator) on a documented one-minute recurring service/timer, with bounded batch size, a database claim/lease or equivalent single-consumer lock, persisted retry eligibility/backoff, and a restart-safe failure record. A failed item remains visible but cannot hot-loop inside one run; a later scheduled run retries it. Print/record selected, appended, replayed, no-op, failed and backlog counts with Site scope; document deployment invocation, ownership, cadence and recovery. The scheduler must not rely on a user opening Financials. Existing price/Finding work uses the same runner. A work item becomes succeeded only after all its selected targets have safely appended/replayed or no-opped; crash and concurrent-run tests must prove eventual drain without duplicate consequence basis.
+5. Keep the consequence read's `CURRENT`/`STALE`/`PENDING`/`HISTORICAL` and typed reasons. Show queued/pending status only when a real unsucceeded work row touches the selected revision; if currentness is stale but no work exists, report that discrepancy explicitly and do not claim queued. S5-01 uses only a `CURRENT`/`PRICED`, same Site/window/FindingRevision/basis consequence after work finishes. No new UI copy or mock panel is authorized here; a necessary owner-facing copy change reopens `USER_REVIEW_REQUIRED` and its checkpoint.

+# S4-02c — consequence work on accepted evidence
+
+Status: implementation-ready
+USER_REVIEW_REQUIRED: false (no new UI or owner-facing copy; independent implementation review required)
+Milestone: S4 Finding + Financials
+Depends on: merged S2-02 and reviewed/merged S4-01, S4-03, S4-02a/b; resolved `A-S4-financial` and `A-S5-overview`. S5-01's current money read depends on this packet's reviewed result.
+Branch when activated: `task/S4-02c-evidence-consequence-work`
+Planner: Codex, 2026-10-14
+
+## Outcome and authority
+
+An accepted late generator-power mean that can alter an existing Site FindingRevision's `fuel-cost-1` input creates durable consequence work in the same database transaction as acceptance. The Site read shows the old consequence as `STALE` (or `PENDING` if no consequence exists) with real queued work, then a scheduled, retryable worker derives and appends the new exact-basis consequence. The S5-01 selected-window read may use money only after that consequence is `CURRENT` and `PRICED` for its selected FindingRevision and window. A fresh stale read alone does not complete this slice.
+
+Authority: `D-2026-10-13-s4-bounded-financial-basis`, `D-2026-10-14-s402-post-review-follow-ons`, `D-2026-10-14-s5-selected-window-overview`, `.agent/architect-S4-02-batch-answers.md` Q2 and `.agent/architect-contest-2026-10-14d-answers.md` (Planner refinement). This is registry node `I-evidence-acceptance-consequence-work`, separate from S4-02a/b and S5-01's UI checkpoint.
+
+Built anchors: `.ai/CODE_STATE.md` S2-02 and S4-02b phases 1/2a/2b; `backend/assetops_backend/evidence/adapters/postgres_evidence_ledger.py` (`process_batch`/`_persist`, accepted evidence and disposition in one transaction), `backend/migrations/versions/0011_financial_consequences.py` (work, attempts and existing triggers), `backend/assetops_backend/financials/{recompute.py,consequence_read.py,adapters/postgres_consequence_store.py}`, and `backend/assetops_backend/recompute_consequences.py`. Reuse `tools/s402b_power_cases.py` and `tools/s402b_fuel_cost_walkthrough.py` as isolated fixture/walkthrough bases. The S4-02b read already detects `TECHNICAL_INPUT_CHANGED` for an unchanged FindingRevision, but acceptance currently enqueues no consequence work; its one-shot CLI has no run schedule.
+
+## Acceptance, work and worker contract
+
+1. Add a migration to extend `financial_consequence_work` with an `EVIDENCE_ACCEPTED` cause and a tenant/Site-scoped FK to the exact `accepted_evidence.id`. Keep existing assumption and FindingRevision causes and rows valid. Each new row identifies the accepted evidence, target Finding and latest eligible FindingRevision at enqueue time, and its half-open affected interval. Constrain cause shape, range, scope and a unique `(accepted_evidence_id, finding_revision_id, cause)` key; duplicates and conflicting evidence create no second row. Index pending selection by Site and due time. Preserve append-only evidence, work and attempt history. Migration upgrade/downgrade and pre-existing rows must be proved.
+2. In the S2-02 acceptance transaction, after a genuinely new accepted evidence ID is returned, select potentially affected existing Site Findings by coarse half-open interval overlap with the accepted interval and the generator-power role. Insert scoped work before commit. If the insert fails, acceptance and its disposition roll back; it must never leave a committed accepted reading with a lost required work row. Exact replay, duplicate, conflict and rejected decisions do not enqueue. If the transaction contains several accepted intervals, each exact accepted ID is deduplicated against its target. Do not trigger on a client-declared role or from a later read. Broad selection may queue a candidate that later no-ops, but must not omit a possibly affected Finding. FindingRevision insertion retains migration 0011's own trigger so findings first created after acceptance also get work.
+3. The worker treats the queued revision as a locator, then rechecks tenant/Site, accepted disposition, bound role/asset, half-open interval overlap, candidate episode/window and the **latest eligible FindingRevision** for that Finding at processing time. Derive against that exact current revision and its accepted public inputs only. A superseded or irrelevant target records a successful typed no-op; if a newer eligible revision exists, process that revision once (its insertion trigger may also queue it). No-op on unrelated roles/assets/windows without appending a consequence. A missing or closed source stays typed and retryable when transient; wrong-Site scope never falls back. Price and technical basis selection remain the reviewed S4-02b contract; no extra amount or quantity shortcut is introduced. The existing unique consequence basis and append lock must make unchanged or repeated work return the existing ID, including concurrent workers and an append-then-crash retry.
+4. Make the run plan operational: extend the server-side CLI to drain a configured tenant/Site (or a scoped active-Site iterator) on a documented one-minute recurring service/timer, with bounded batch size, a database claim/lease or equivalent single-consumer lock, persisted retry eligibility/backoff, and a restart-safe failure record. A failed item remains visible but cannot hot-loop inside one run; a later scheduled run retries it. Print/record selected, appended, replayed, no-op, failed and backlog counts with Site scope; document deployment invocation, ownership, cadence and recovery. The scheduler must not rely on a user opening Financials. Existing price/Finding work uses the same runner. A work item becomes succeeded only after all its selected targets have safely appended/replayed or no-opped; crash and concurrent-run tests must prove eventual drain without duplicate consequence basis.
+5. Keep the consequence read's `CURRENT`/`STALE`/`PENDING`/`HISTORICAL` and typed reasons. Show queued/pending status only when a real unsucceeded work row touches the selected revision; if currentness is stale but no work exists, report that discrepancy explicitly and do not claim queued. S5-01 uses only a `CURRENT`/`PRICED`, same Site/window/FindingRevision/basis consequence after work finishes. No new UI copy or mock panel is authorized here; a necessary owner-facing copy change reopens `USER_REVIEW_REQUIRED` and its checkpoint.
+
+## Phases and focused proof
+
+Each phase fits one Claude Implementer context below approximately 120k tokens and receives an independent fresh review before the next.
+
+| Phase | Reviewable result and focused proof |
+| --- | --- |
+| 1. Transactional acceptance work | Migration, scoped accepted-evidence FK/uniqueness, acceptance integration. Postgres tests prove committed accepted late power plus one work row, rollback atomicity, exact retry/duplicate/conflict/rejection, unrelated Site and zero-overlap, half-open edge, and existing migration 0011 causes/backfill. |
+| 2. Scoped drain and run plan | Role/asset/window/latest-revision recheck, typed no-op, idempotent append, claim/retry/backoff and recurring runner instructions. Test irrelevant accepted input, revised Finding between enqueue and drain, wrong Site, two workers, failure then scheduled retry, append-then-crash, restart and bounded batch; inspect exact work/attempt/consequence IDs and no duplicate basis. |
+| 3. Late-power end-to-end walkthrough | On an isolated Postgres copy of the S4-02b power fixture, first persist an exact FindingRevision and consequence, then accept a **late** good generator-power interval that changes its technical digest without relying on a new FindingRevision. Before the scheduled drain, assert `STALE/TECHNICAL_INPUT_CHANGED` and the queued work ID (or `PENDING` with work when no head); after drain, assert new consequence revision, changed accepted-evidence/technical digest, same or explicitly superseded eligible FindingRevision, old version retained, current priced eligibility for S5-01, and reload stability. Include an unrelated accepted reading that succeeds as no-op. Record commands and IDs, not illustrative mock money. |
+
+Reviewer checks migration safety, DB transaction rollback, scope/foreign Site refusal, half-open boundaries, accepted evidence identity, coarse-selection completeness, latest eligible revision, public-only lineage, no-op, retry and currentness. Run focused Postgres/API/model tests, the existing S4-02b walkthrough variant and applicable workflow guards; run `tools/check-all.ps1` when dependencies are installed. Review independently before registry resolution. No separate owner visual checkpoint is needed while this remains non-UI; S5-01 retains its own `USER_REVIEW_REQUIRED` checkpoint.
+
+Out of scope: new fuel model or price semantics, altered S4-02b copy/layout, source-authorship provenance (separate `I-stored-demo-provenance`), equal-start price succession, Assumptions Site consequence history, S5 Overview implementation, private simulator truth, and the owner's broader [analysis input data for simulated and real Sites](../.ai/MILESTONE_REVIEW_BACKLOG.md#owner-analysis-input-data-for-simulated-and-real-sites-2026-10-14) backlog item. This packet proves a late accepted input changes a consequence; it does not fix ordinary gateway power cadence or real-Site input readiness.
