+# S4-02c — consequence work on accepted evidence
+
+Status: implementation-ready
+USER_REVIEW_REQUIRED: false (no new UI or owner-facing copy; independent implementation review required)
+Milestone: S4 Finding + Financials
+Depends on: merged S2-02 and reviewed/merged S4-01, S4-03, S4-02a/b; resolved `A-S4-financial` and `A-S5-overview`. S5-01's current money read depends on this packet's reviewed result.
+Branch when activated: `task/S4-02c-evidence-consequence-work`
+Planner: Codex, 2026-10-14
+
+## Outcome and authority
+
+An accepted late generator-power mean that can alter an existing Site FindingRevision's `fuel-cost-1` input creates durable consequence work in the same database transaction as acceptance. The Site read shows the old consequence as `STALE` (or `PENDING` if no consequence exists) with real queued work, then a scheduled, retryable worker derives and appends the new exact-basis consequence. The S5-01 selected-window read may use money only after that consequence is `CURRENT` and `PRICED` for its selected FindingRevision and window. A fresh stale read alone does not complete this slice.
+
+Authority: `D-2026-10-13-s4-bounded-financial-basis`, `D-2026-10-14-s402-post-review-follow-ons`, `D-2026-10-14-s5-selected-window-overview`, `.agent/architect-S4-02-batch-answers.md` Q2 and `.agent/architect-contest-2026-10-14d-answers.md` (Planner refinement). This is registry node `I-evidence-acceptance-consequence-work`, separate from S4-02a/b and S5-01's UI checkpoint.
+
+Built anchors: `.ai/CODE_STATE.md` S2-02 and S4-02b phases 1/2a/2b; `backend/assetops_backend/evidence/adapters/postgres_evidence_ledger.py` (`process_batch`/`_persist`, accepted evidence and disposition in one transaction), `backend/migrations/versions/0011_financial_consequences.py` (work, attempts and existing triggers), `backend/assetops_backend/financials/{recompute.py,consequence_read.py,adapters/postgres_consequence_store.py}`, and `backend/assetops_backend/recompute_consequences.py`. Reuse `tools/s402b_power_cases.py` and `tools/s402b_fuel_cost_walkthrough.py` as isolated fixture/walkthrough bases. The S4-02b read already detects `TECHNICAL_INPUT_CHANGED` for an unchanged FindingRevision, but acceptance currently enqueues no consequence work; its one-shot CLI has no run schedule.
+
+## Acceptance, work and worker contract
+
+1. Add a migration to extend `financial_consequence_work` with an `EVIDENCE_ACCEPTED` cause and a tenant/Site-scoped FK to the exact `accepted_evidence.id`. Keep existing assumption and FindingRevision causes and rows valid. Each new row identifies the accepted evidence, target Finding and latest eligible FindingRevision at enqueue time, and its half-open affected interval. Constrain cause shape, range, scope and a unique `(accepted_evidence_id, finding_revision_id, cause)` key; duplicates and conflicting evidence create no second row. Index pending selection by Site and due time. Preserve append-only evidence, work and attempt history. Migration upgrade/downgrade and pre-existing rows must be proved.
+2. In the S2-02 acceptance transaction, after a genuinely new accepted evidence ID is returned, select potentially affected existing Site Findings by coarse half-open interval overlap with the accepted interval and the generator-power role. Insert scoped work before commit. If the insert fails, acceptance and its disposition roll back; it must never leave a committed accepted reading with a lost required work row. Exact replay, duplicate, conflict and rejected decisions do not enqueue. If the transaction contains several accepted intervals, each exact accepted ID is deduplicated against its target. Do not trigger on a client-declared role or from a later read. Broad selection may queue a candidate that later no-ops, but must not omit a possibly affected Finding. FindingRevision insertion retains migration 0011's own trigger so findings first created after acceptance also get work.
+3. The worker treats the queued revision as a locator, then rechecks tenant/Site, accepted disposition, bound role/asset, half-open interval overlap, candidate episode/window and the **latest eligible FindingRevision** for that Finding at processing time. Derive against that exact current revision and its accepted public inputs only. A superseded or irrelevant target records a successful typed no-op; if a newer eligible revision exists, process that revision once (its insertion trigger may also queue it). No-op on unrelated roles/assets/windows without appending a consequence. A missing or closed source stays typed and retryable when transient; wrong-Site scope never falls back. Price and technical basis selection remain the reviewed S4-02b contract; no extra amount or quantity shortcut is introduced. The existing unique consequence basis and append lock must make unchanged or repeated work return the existing ID, including concurrent workers and an append-then-crash retry.
+4. Make the run plan operational: extend the server-side CLI to drain a configured tenant/Site (or a scoped active-Site iterator) on a documented one-minute recurring service/timer, with bounded batch size, a database claim/lease or equivalent single-consumer lock, persisted retry eligibility/backoff, and a restart-safe failure record. A failed item remains visible but cannot hot-loop inside one run; a later scheduled run retries it. Print/record selected, appended, replayed, no-op, failed and backlog counts with Site scope; document deployment invocation, ownership, cadence and recovery. The scheduler must not rely on a user opening Financials. Existing price/Finding work uses the same runner. A work item becomes succeeded only after all its selected targets have safely appended/replayed or no-opped; crash and concurrent-run tests must prove eventual drain without duplicate consequence basis.
+5. Keep the consequence read's `CURRENT`/`STALE`/`PENDING`/`HISTORICAL` and typed reasons. Show queued/pending status only when a real unsucceeded work row touches the selected revision; if currentness is stale but no work exists, report that discrepancy explicitly and do not claim queued. S5-01 uses only a `CURRENT`/`PRICED`, same Site/window/FindingRevision/basis consequence after work finishes. No new UI copy or mock panel is authorized here; a necessary owner-facing copy change reopens `USER_REVIEW_REQUIRED` and its checkpoint.
+
+## Phases and focused proof
+
+Each phase fits one Claude Implementer context below approximately 120k tokens and receives an independent fresh review before the next.
+
+| Phase | Reviewable result and focused proof |
+| --- | --- |
+| 1. Transactional acceptance work | Migration, scoped accepted-evidence FK/uniqueness, acceptance integration. Postgres tests prove committed accepted late power plus one work row, rollback atomicity, exact retry/duplicate/conflict/rejection, unrelated Site and zero-overlap, half-open edge, and existing migration 0011 causes/backfill. |
+| 2. Scoped drain and run plan | Role/asset/window/latest-revision recheck, typed no-op, idempotent append, claim/retry/backoff and recurring runner instructions. Test irrelevant accepted input, revised Finding between enqueue and drain, wrong Site, two workers, failure then scheduled retry, append-then-crash, restart and bounded batch; inspect exact work/attempt/consequence IDs and no duplicate basis. |
+| 3. Late-power end-to-end walkthrough | On an isolated Postgres copy of the S4-02b power fixture, first persist an exact FindingRevision and consequence, then accept a **late** good generator-power interval that changes its technical digest without relying on a new FindingRevision. Before the scheduled drain, assert `STALE/TECHNICAL_INPUT_CHANGED` and the queued work ID (or `PENDING` with work when no head); after drain, assert new consequence revision, changed accepted-evidence/technical digest, same or explicitly superseded eligible FindingRevision, old version retained, current priced eligibility for S5-01, and reload stability. Include an unrelated accepted reading that succeeds as no-op. Record commands and IDs, not illustrative mock money. |
+
+Reviewer checks migration safety, DB transaction rollback, scope/foreign Site refusal, half-open boundaries, accepted evidence identity, coarse-selection completeness, latest eligible revision, public-only lineage, no-op, retry and currentness. Run focused Postgres/API/model tests, the existing S4-02b walkthrough variant and applicable workflow guards; run `tools/check-all.ps1` when dependencies are installed. Review independently before registry resolution. No separate owner visual checkpoint is needed while this remains non-UI; S5-01 retains its own `USER_REVIEW_REQUIRED` checkpoint.
+
+Out of scope: new fuel model or price semantics, altered S4-02b copy/layout, source-authorship provenance (separate `I-stored-demo-provenance`), equal-start price succession, Assumptions Site consequence history, S5 Overview implementation, private simulator truth, and the owner's broader [analysis input data for simulated and real Sites](../.ai/MILESTONE_REVIEW_BACKLOG.md#owner-analysis-input-data-for-simulated-and-real-sites-2026-10-14) backlog item. This packet proves a late accepted input changes a consequence; it does not fix ordinary gateway power cadence or real-Site input readiness.

17:function parseQueue(readme) {
function packetMeta(text) {
  const status = (text.match(/^Status:\s*(.*)$/m) || [])[1];
  const review = (text.match(/^USER_REVIEW_REQUIRED:\s*(.*)$/m) || [])[1];
  return {status: status?.trim() ?? null, user_review_required: review ? !/^false\b/i.test(review.trim()) : null};
}

const packetPhase = (status) => {
  if (!status) return 'unknown';
  if (/^done\b/i.test(status)) return 'done';
  if (/^in_review\b/i.test(status)) return 'in_review';
  if (/^(active|in_progress|in progress)\b/i.test(status)) return 'active';
  if (/^(outline|executable|carry|implementation-ready|refined|open)\b/i.test(status) || /^umbrella\/index\b/i.test(status) || /not activated/i.test(status)) return 'not_started';
  return 'unknown';
};

// ---- fingerprints ----------------------------------------------------------

// Line endings are normalised so a CRLF checkout and an LF working copy agree.
const sha = (text) => crypto.createHash('sha256').update(text.replace(/\r\n/g, '\n')).digest('hex').slice(0, 16);
function fingerprints(inputs) {
  // inputs: {registry, queue, packet_status, panel_contracts, manifest, owner_input} as raw strings
  return Object.fromEntries(Object.entries(inputs).map(([key, text]) => [key, sha(text)]));
}
function staleInputs(expected, actual) {
  return Object.keys({...expected, ...actual}).filter((key) => expected[key] !== actual[key]);
}

// ---- graph helpers ---------------------------------------------------------

function graph(registry) {
  const nodes = new Map(registry.nodes.map((node) => [node.id, node]));
  const memo = new Map();
  const ancestors = (id) => {
    if (memo.has(id)) return memo.get(id);
    const out = new Set();
    for (const dep of nodes.get(id)?.requires || []) {
      out.add(dep);
      for (const a of ancestors(dep)) out.add(a);
    }
    memo.set(id, out);
    return out;
  };
  const isOpen = (id) => nodes.get(id)?.status === 'open';
  // Open gates needed to close `ids`: the ids themselves and every open ancestor.
  const openClosure = (ids) => {
    const out = new Set();
    for (const id of ids) for (const x of [id, ...ancestors(id)]) if (isOpen(x)) out.add(x);
    return out;
  };
  return {nodes, ancestors, isOpen, openClosure};
}

+# S4-02c — consequence work on accepted evidence
+
+Status: implementation-ready
+USER_REVIEW_REQUIRED: false (no new UI or owner-facing copy; independent implementation review required)
+Milestone: S4 Finding + Financials
+Depends on: merged S2-02 and reviewed/merged S4-01, S4-03, S4-02a/b; resolved `A-S4-financial` and `A-S5-overview`. S5-01's current money read depends on this packet's reviewed result.
+Branch when activated: `task/S4-02c-evidence-consequence-work`
+Planner: Codex, 2026-10-14
+
+## Outcome and authority
+
+An accepted late generator-power mean that can alter an existing Site FindingRevision's `fuel-cost-1` input creates durable consequence work in the same database transaction as acceptance. The Site read shows the old consequence as `STALE` (or `PENDING` if no consequence exists) with real queued work, then a scheduled, retryable worker derives and appends the new exact-basis consequence. The S5-01 selected-window read may use money only after that consequence is `CURRENT` and `PRICED` for its selected FindingRevision and window. A fresh stale read alone does not complete this slice.
+
+Authority: `D-2026-10-13-s4-bounded-financial-basis`, `D-2026-10-14-s402-post-review-follow-ons`, `D-2026-10-14-s5-selected-window-overview`, `.agent/architect-S4-02-batch-answers.md` Q2 and `.agent/architect-contest-2026-10-14d-answers.md` (Planner refinement). This is registry node `I-evidence-acceptance-consequence-work`, separate from S4-02a/b and S5-01's UI checkpoint.
+
+Built anchors: `.ai/CODE_STATE.md` S2-02 and S4-02b phases 1/2a/2b; `backend/assetops_backend/evidence/adapters/postgres_evidence_ledger.py` (`process_batch`/`_persist`, accepted evidence and disposition in one transaction), `backend/migrations/versions/0011_financial_consequences.py` (work, attempts and existing triggers), `backend/assetops_backend/financials/{recompute.py,consequence_read.py,adapters/postgres_consequence_store.py}`, and `backend/assetops_backend/recompute_consequences.py`. Reuse `tools/s402b_power_cases.py` and `tools/s402b_fuel_cost_walkthrough.py` as isolated fixture/walkthrough bases. The S4-02b read already detects `TECHNICAL_INPUT_CHANGED` for an unchanged FindingRevision, but acceptance currently enqueues no consequence work; its one-shot CLI has no run schedule.
+
+## Acceptance, work and worker contract
+
+1. Add a migration to extend `financial_consequence_work` with an `EVIDENCE_ACCEPTED` cause and a tenant/Site-scoped FK to the exact `accepted_evidence.id`. Keep existing assumption and FindingRevision causes and rows valid. Each new row identifies the accepted evidence, target Finding and latest eligible FindingRevision at enqueue time, and its half-open affected interval. Constrain cause shape, range, scope and a unique `(accepted_evidence_id, finding_revision_id, cause)` key; duplicates and conflicting evidence create no second row. Index pending selection by Site and due time. Preserve append-only evidence, work and attempt history. Migration upgrade/downgrade and pre-existing rows must be proved.
+2. In the S2-02 acceptance transaction, after a genuinely new accepted evidence ID is returned, select potentially affected existing Site Findings by coarse half-open interval overlap with the accepted interval and the generator-power role. Insert scoped work before commit. If the insert fails, acceptance and its disposition roll back; it must never leave a committed accepted reading with a lost required work row. Exact replay, duplicate, conflict and rejected decisions do not enqueue. If the transaction contains several accepted intervals, each exact accepted ID is deduplicated against its target. Do not trigger on a client-declared role or from a later read. Broad selection may queue a candidate that later no-ops, but must not omit a possibly affected Finding. FindingRevision insertion retains migration 0011's own trigger so findings first created after acceptance also get work.
+3. The worker treats the queued revision as a locator, then rechecks tenant/Site, accepted disposition, bound role/asset, half-open interval overlap, candidate episode/window and the **latest eligible FindingRevision** for that Finding at processing time. Derive against that exact current revision and its accepted public inputs only. A superseded or irrelevant target records a successful typed no-op; if a newer eligible revision exists, process that revision once (its insertion trigger may also queue it). No-op on unrelated roles/assets/windows without appending a consequence. A missing or closed source stays typed and retryable when transient; wrong-Site scope never falls back. Price and technical basis selection remain the reviewed S4-02b contract; no extra amount or quantity shortcut is introduced. The existing unique consequence basis and append lock must make unchanged or repeated work return the existing ID, including concurrent workers and an append-then-crash retry.
+4. Make the run plan operational: extend the server-side CLI to drain a configured tenant/Site (or a scoped active-Site iterator) on a documented one-minute recurring service/timer, with bounded batch size, a database claim/lease or equivalent single-consumer lock, persisted retry eligibility/backoff, and a restart-safe failure record. A failed item remains visible but cannot hot-loop inside one run; a later scheduled run retries it. Print/record selected, appended, replayed, no-op, failed and backlog counts with Site scope; document deployment invocation, ownership, cadence and recovery. The scheduler must not rely on a user opening Financials. Existing price/Finding work uses the same runner. A work item becomes succeeded only after all its selected targets have safely appended/replayed or no-opped; crash and concurrent-run tests must prove eventual drain without duplicate consequence basis.
+5. Keep the consequence read's `CURRENT`/`STALE`/`PENDING`/`HISTORICAL` and typed reasons. Show queued/pending status only when a real unsucceeded work row touches the selected revision; if currentness is stale but no work exists, report that discrepancy explicitly and do not claim queued. S5-01 uses only a `CURRENT`/`PRICED`, same Site/window/FindingRevision/basis consequence after work finishes. No new UI copy or mock panel is authorized here; a necessary owner-facing copy change reopens `USER_REVIEW_REQUIRED` and its checkpoint.
+
+## Phases and focused proof
+
+Each phase fits one Claude Implementer context below approximately 120k tokens and receives an independent fresh review before the next.
+
+| Phase | Reviewable result and focused proof |
+| --- | --- |
+| 1. Transactional acceptance work | Migration, scoped accepted-evidence FK/uniqueness, acceptance integration. Postgres tests prove committed accepted late power plus one work row, rollback atomicity, exact retry/duplicate/conflict/rejection, unrelated Site and zero-overlap, half-open edge, and existing migration 0011 causes/backfill. |
+| 2. Scoped drain and run plan | Role/asset/window/latest-revision recheck, typed no-op, idempotent append, claim/retry/backoff and recurring runner instructions. Test irrelevant accepted input, revised Finding between enqueue and drain, wrong Site, two workers, failure then scheduled retry, append-then-crash, restart and bounded batch; inspect exact work/attempt/consequence IDs and no duplicate basis. |
+| 3. Late-power end-to-end walkthrough | On an isolated Postgres copy of the S4-02b power fixture, first persist an exact FindingRevision and consequence, then accept a **late** good generator-power interval that changes its technical digest without relying on a new FindingRevision. Before the scheduled drain, assert `STALE/TECHNICAL_INPUT_CHANGED` and the queued work ID (or `PENDING` with work when no head); after drain, assert new consequence revision, changed accepted-evidence/technical digest, same or explicitly superseded eligible FindingRevision, old version retained, current priced eligibility for S5-01, and reload stability. Include an unrelated accepted reading that succeeds as no-op. Record commands and IDs, not illustrative mock money. |
+
+Reviewer checks migration safety, DB transaction rollback, scope/foreign Site refusal, half-open boundaries, accepted evidence identity, coarse-selection completeness, latest eligible revision, public-only lineage, no-op, retry and currentness. Run focused Postgres/API/model tests, the existing S4-02b walkthrough variant and applicable workflow guards; run `tools/check-all.ps1` when dependencies are installed. Review independently before registry resolution. No separate owner visual checkpoint is needed while this remains non-UI; S5-01 retains its own `USER_REVIEW_REQUIRED` checkpoint.
+
+Out of scope: new fuel model or price semantics, altered S4-02b copy/layout, source-authorship provenance (separate `I-stored-demo-provenance`), equal-start price succession, Assumptions Site consequence history, S5 Overview implementation, private simulator truth, and the owner's broader [analysis input data for simulated and real Sites](../.ai/MILESTONE_REVIEW_BACKLOG.md#owner-analysis-input-data-for-simulated-and-real-sites-2026-10-14) backlog item. This packet proves a late accepted input changes a consequence; it does not fix ordinary gateway power cadence or real-Site input readiness.

// Delivery-plan validation and the deterministic `next-work` report (PRE-S3-03).
// Implements D-2026-10-09-owner-delivery-strategy "Selection within the active wave".
// Pure functions over already-loaded inputs, so fixtures can exercise every refusal;
// check_v69_dependency_registry.cjs supplies the real files.
const crypto = require('node:crypto');
const mockGaps = require('./mock_gaps.cjs');

const PORTION_STATES = ['delivered', 'open', 'unmapped', 'excluded'];
const VARIANTS = ['bounded', 'positive', 'unknown'];

// ---- task discovery --------------------------------------------------------

// S1-S7 queue rows: `| S<n> ... | [S<n>-NN<x>](packet.md) | ... | status |`.
function parseQueue(readme) {
  return [...readme.matchAll(/^\|\s*S[1-7][^|]*\|\s*\[(S[1-7]-\d{2}[a-z]?)\]\(([^)]+)\)[^\n]*$/gm)]
    .map((m) => ({task: m[1], packet: m[2]}));
}

// Every packet linked anywhere in tasks/README.md (PRE-S#-##, V-01*, S2-02r, S3-02, S4-03, any future packet) counts
// for the global stop: an active or in-review one stops selection (Architect Q7). nextWork drops ids already
// covered by registry task nodes.
function parseGateQueue(readme) {
  const seen = new Map();
  // Discover by link target filename (any label); a bare-id link text is the fallback for non-conforming filenames.
  const idRe = String.raw`[A-Z][A-Za-z0-9]*(?:-[A-Z]\d)?-\d{2}[a-z]?`;
  const fileRe = new RegExp('^(' + idRe + String.raw`)(?:-[^/]*)?\.md$`);
  const textRe = new RegExp('^' + idRe + '$');
  for (const m of readme.matchAll(/\[([^\]\n]*)\]\(([^)#\s]+\.md)\)/g)) {
    if (/^[a-z]+:\/\//i.test(m[2])) continue;
    const id = (m[2].split('/').pop().match(fileRe) || [])[1] || (textRe.test(m[1]) ? m[1] : null);
    if (id && !seen.has(id)) seen.set(id, {task: id, packet: m[2]});
  }
  return [...seen.values()];
}

+# S4-02c — consequence work on accepted evidence
+
+Status: implementation-ready
+USER_REVIEW_REQUIRED: false (no new UI or owner-facing copy; independent implementation review required)
+Milestone: S4 Finding + Financials
+Depends on: merged S2-02 and reviewed/merged S4-01, S4-03, S4-02a/b; resolved `A-S4-financial` and `A-S5-overview`. S5-01's current money read depends on this packet's reviewed result.
+Branch when activated: `task/S4-02c-evidence-consequence-work`
+Planner: Codex, 2026-10-14
+
+## Outcome and authority
+
+An accepted late generator-power mean that can alter an existing Site FindingRevision's `fuel-cost-1` input creates durable consequence work in the same database transaction as acceptance. The Site read shows the old consequence as `STALE` (or `PENDING` if no consequence exists) with real queued work, then a scheduled, retryable worker derives and appends the new exact-basis consequence. The S5-01 selected-window read may use money only after that consequence is `CURRENT` and `PRICED` for its selected FindingRevision and window. A fresh stale read alone does not complete this slice.
+
+Authority: `D-2026-10-13-s4-bounded-financial-basis`, `D-2026-10-14-s402-post-review-follow-ons`, `D-2026-10-14-s5-selected-window-overview`, `.agent/architect-S4-02-batch-answers.md` Q2 and `.agent/architect-contest-2026-10-14d-answers.md` (Planner refinement). This is registry node `I-evidence-acceptance-consequence-work`, separate from S4-02a/b and S5-01's UI checkpoint.
+
+Built anchors: `.ai/CODE_STATE.md` S2-02 and S4-02b phases 1/2a/2b; `backend/assetops_backend/evidence/adapters/postgres_evidence_ledger.py` (`process_batch`/`_persist`, accepted evidence and disposition in one transaction), `backend/migrations/versions/0011_financial_consequences.py` (work, attempts and existing triggers), `backend/assetops_backend/financials/{recompute.py,consequence_read.py,adapters/postgres_consequence_store.py}`, and `backend/assetops_backend/recompute_consequences.py`. Reuse `tools/s402b_power_cases.py` and `tools/s402b_fuel_cost_walkthrough.py` as isolated fixture/walkthrough bases. The S4-02b read already detects `TECHNICAL_INPUT_CHANGED` for an unchanged FindingRevision, but acceptance currently enqueues no consequence work; its one-shot CLI has no run schedule.
+
+## Acceptance, work and worker contract
+
+1. Add a migration to extend `financial_consequence_work` with an `EVIDENCE_ACCEPTED` cause and a tenant/Site-scoped FK to the exact `accepted_evidence.id`. Keep existing assumption and FindingRevision causes and rows valid. Each new row identifies the accepted evidence, target Finding and latest eligible FindingRevision at enqueue time, and its half-open affected interval. Constrain cause shape, range, scope and a unique `(accepted_evidence_id, finding_revision_id, cause)` key; duplicates and conflicting evidence create no second row. Index pending selection by Site and due time. Preserve append-only evidence, work and attempt history. Migration upgrade/downgrade and pre-existing rows must be proved.
+2. In the S2-02 acceptance transaction, after a genuinely new accepted evidence ID is returned, select potentially affected existing Site Findings by coarse half-open interval overlap with the accepted interval and the generator-power role. Insert scoped work before commit. If the insert fails, acceptance and its disposition roll back; it must never leave a committed accepted reading with a lost required work row. Exact replay, duplicate, conflict and rejected decisions do not enqueue. If the transaction contains several accepted intervals, each exact accepted ID is deduplicated against its target. Do not trigger on a client-declared role or from a later read. Broad selection may queue a candidate that later no-ops, but must not omit a possibly affected Finding. FindingRevision insertion retains migration 0011's own trigger so findings first created after acceptance also get work.
+3. The worker treats the queued revision as a locator, then rechecks tenant/Site, accepted disposition, bound role/asset, half-open interval overlap, candidate episode/window and the **latest eligible FindingRevision** for that Finding at processing time. Derive against that exact current revision and its accepted public inputs only. A superseded or irrelevant target records a successful typed no-op; if a newer eligible revision exists, process that revision once (its insertion trigger may also queue it). No-op on unrelated roles/assets/windows without appending a consequence. A missing or closed source stays typed and retryable when transient; wrong-Site scope never falls back. Price and technical basis selection remain the reviewed S4-02b contract; no extra amount or quantity shortcut is introduced. The existing unique consequence basis and append lock must make unchanged or repeated work return the existing ID, including concurrent workers and an append-then-crash retry.
+4. Make the run plan operational: extend the server-side CLI to drain a configured tenant/Site (or a scoped active-Site iterator) on a documented one-minute recurring service/timer, with bounded batch size, a database claim/lease or equivalent single-consumer lock, persisted retry eligibility/backoff, and a restart-safe failure record. A failed item remains visible but cannot hot-loop inside one run; a later scheduled run retries it. Print/record selected, appended, replayed, no-op, failed and backlog counts with Site scope; document deployment invocation, ownership, cadence and recovery. The scheduler must not rely on a user opening Financials. Existing price/Finding work uses the same runner. A work item becomes succeeded only after all its selected targets have safely appended/replayed or no-opped; crash and concurrent-run tests must prove eventual drain without duplicate consequence basis.
+5. Keep the consequence read's `CURRENT`/`STALE`/`PENDING`/`HISTORICAL` and typed reasons. Show queued/pending status only when a real unsucceeded work row touches the selected revision; if currentness is stale but no work exists, report that discrepancy explicitly and do not claim queued. S5-01 uses only a `CURRENT`/`PRICED`, same Site/window/FindingRevision/basis consequence after work finishes. No new UI copy or mock panel is authorized here; a necessary owner-facing copy change reopens `USER_REVIEW_REQUIRED` and its checkpoint.
+
+## Phases and focused proof
+
+Each phase fits one Claude Implementer context below approximately 120k tokens and receives an independent fresh review before the next.
+
+| Phase | Reviewable result and focused proof |
+| --- | --- |
+| 1. Transactional acceptance work | Migration, scoped accepted-evidence FK/uniqueness, acceptance integration. Postgres tests prove committed accepted late power plus one work row, rollback atomicity, exact retry/duplicate/conflict/rejection, unrelated Site and zero-overlap, half-open edge, and existing migration 0011 causes/backfill. |
+| 2. Scoped drain and run plan | Role/asset/window/latest-revision recheck, typed no-op, idempotent append, claim/retry/backoff and recurring runner instructions. Test irrelevant accepted input, revised Finding between enqueue and drain, wrong Site, two workers, failure then scheduled retry, append-then-crash, restart and bounded batch; inspect exact work/attempt/consequence IDs and no duplicate basis. |
+| 3. Late-power end-to-end walkthrough | On an isolated Postgres copy of the S4-02b power fixture, first persist an exact FindingRevision and consequence, then accept a **late** good generator-power interval that changes its technical digest without relying on a new FindingRevision. Before the scheduled drain, assert `STALE/TECHNICAL_INPUT_CHANGED` and the queued work ID (or `PENDING` with work when no head); after drain, assert new consequence revision, changed accepted-evidence/technical digest, same or explicitly superseded eligible FindingRevision, old version retained, current priced eligibility for S5-01, and reload stability. Include an unrelated accepted reading that succeeds as no-op. Record commands and IDs, not illustrative mock money. |
+
+Reviewer checks migration safety, DB transaction rollback, scope/foreign Site refusal, half-open boundaries, accepted evidence identity, coarse-selection completeness, latest eligible revision, public-only lineage, no-op, retry and currentness. Run focused Postgres/API/model tests, the existing S4-02b walkthrough variant and applicable workflow guards; run `tools/check-all.ps1` when dependencies are installed. Review independently before registry resolution. No separate owner visual checkpoint is needed while this remains non-UI; S5-01 retains its own `USER_REVIEW_REQUIRED` checkpoint.
+
+Out of scope: new fuel model or price semantics, altered S4-02b copy/layout, source-authorship provenance (separate `I-stored-demo-provenance`), equal-start price succession, Assumptions Site consequence history, S5 Overview implementation, private simulator truth, and the owner's broader [analysis input data for simulated and real Sites](../.ai/MILESTONE_REVIEW_BACKLOG.md#owner-analysis-input-data-for-simulated-and-real-sites-2026-10-14) backlog item. This packet proves a late accepted input changes a consequence; it does not fix ordinary gateway power cadence or real-Site input readiness.

+# S4-02c — consequence work on accepted evidence
+
+Status: implementation-ready
+USER_REVIEW_REQUIRED: false (no new UI or owner-facing copy; independent implementation review required)
+Milestone: S4 Finding + Financials
+Depends on: merged S2-02 and reviewed/merged S4-01, S4-03, S4-02a/b; resolved `A-S4-financial` and `A-S5-overview`. S5-01's current money read depends on this packet's reviewed result.
+Branch when activated: `task/S4-02c-evidence-consequence-work`
+Planner: Codex, 2026-10-14
+
+## Outcome and authority
+
+An accepted late generator-power mean that can alter an existing Site FindingRevision's `fuel-cost-1` input creates durable consequence work in the same database transaction as acceptance. The Site read shows the old consequence as `STALE` (or `PENDING` if no consequence exists) with real queued work, then a scheduled, retryable worker derives and appends the new exact-basis consequence. The S5-01 selected-window read may use money only after that consequence is `CURRENT` and `PRICED` for its selected FindingRevision and window. A fresh stale read alone does not complete this slice.
+
+Authority: `D-2026-10-13-s4-bounded-financial-basis`, `D-2026-10-14-s402-post-review-follow-ons`, `D-2026-10-14-s5-selected-window-overview`, `.agent/architect-S4-02-batch-answers.md` Q2 and `.agent/architect-contest-2026-10-14d-answers.md` (Planner refinement). This is registry node `I-evidence-acceptance-consequence-work`, separate from S4-02a/b and S5-01's UI checkpoint.
+
+Built anchors: `.ai/CODE_STATE.md` S2-02 and S4-02b phases 1/2a/2b; `backend/assetops_backend/evidence/adapters/postgres_evidence_ledger.py` (`process_batch`/`_persist`, accepted evidence and disposition in one transaction), `backend/migrations/versions/0011_financial_consequences.py` (work, attempts and existing triggers), `backend/assetops_backend/financials/{recompute.py,consequence_read.py,adapters/postgres_consequence_store.py}`, and `backend/assetops_backend/recompute_consequences.py`. Reuse `tools/s402b_power_cases.py` and `tools/s402b_fuel_cost_walkthrough.py` as isolated fixture/walkthrough bases. The S4-02b read already detects `TECHNICAL_INPUT_CHANGED` for an unchanged FindingRevision, but acceptance currently enqueues no consequence work; its one-shot CLI has no run schedule.
+
+## Acceptance, work and worker contract
+
+1. Add a migration to extend `financial_consequence_work` with an `EVIDENCE_ACCEPTED` cause and a tenant/Site-scoped FK to the exact `accepted_evidence.id`. Keep existing assumption and FindingRevision causes and rows valid. Each new row identifies the accepted evidence, target Finding and latest eligible FindingRevision at enqueue time, and its half-open affected interval. Constrain cause shape, range, scope and a unique `(accepted_evidence_id, finding_revision_id, cause)` key; duplicates and conflicting evidence create no second row. Index pending selection by Site and due time. Preserve append-only evidence, work and attempt history. Migration upgrade/downgrade and pre-existing rows must be proved.
+2. In the S2-02 acceptance transaction, after a genuinely new accepted evidence ID is returned, select potentially affected existing Site Findings by coarse half-open interval overlap with the accepted interval and the generator-power role. Insert scoped work before commit. If the insert fails, acceptance and its disposition roll back; it must never leave a committed accepted reading with a lost required work row. Exact replay, duplicate, conflict and rejected decisions do not enqueue. If the transaction contains several accepted intervals, each exact accepted ID is deduplicated against its target. Do not trigger on a client-declared role or from a later read. Broad selection may queue a candidate that later no-ops, but must not omit a possibly affected Finding. FindingRevision insertion retains migration 0011's own trigger so findings first created after acceptance also get work.
+3. The worker treats the queued revision as a locator, then rechecks tenant/Site, accepted disposition, bound role/asset, half-open interval overlap, candidate episode/window and the **latest eligible FindingRevision** for that Finding at processing time. Derive against that exact current revision and its accepted public inputs only. A superseded or irrelevant target records a successful typed no-op; if a newer eligible revision exists, process that revision once (its insertion trigger may also queue it). No-op on unrelated roles/assets/windows without appending a consequence. A missing or closed source stays typed and retryable when transient; wrong-Site scope never falls back. Price and technical basis selection remain the reviewed S4-02b contract; no extra amount or quantity shortcut is introduced. The existing unique consequence basis and append lock must make unchanged or repeated work return the existing ID, including concurrent workers and an append-then-crash retry.
+4. Make the run plan operational: extend the server-side CLI to drain a configured tenant/Site (or a scoped active-Site iterator) on a documented one-minute recurring service/timer, with bounded batch size, a database claim/lease or equivalent single-consumer lock, persisted retry eligibility/backoff, and a restart-safe failure record. A failed item remains visible but cannot hot-loop inside one run; a later scheduled run retries it. Print/record selected, appended, replayed, no-op, failed and backlog counts with Site scope; document deployment invocation, ownership, cadence and recovery. The scheduler must not rely on a user opening Financials. Existing price/Finding work uses the same runner. A work item becomes succeeded only after all its selected targets have safely appended/replayed or no-opped; crash and concurrent-run tests must prove eventual drain without duplicate consequence basis.
+5. Keep the consequence read's `CURRENT`/`STALE`/`PENDING`/`HISTORICAL` and typed reasons. Show queued/pending status only when a real unsucceeded work row touches the selected revision; if currentness is stale but no work exists, report that discrepancy explicitly and do not claim queued. S5-01 uses only a `CURRENT`/`PRICED`, same Site/window/FindingRevision/basis consequence after work finishes. No new UI copy or mock panel is authorized here; a necessary owner-facing copy change reopens `USER_REVIEW_REQUIRED` and its checkpoint.
+
+## Phases and focused proof
+
+Each phase fits one Claude Implementer context below approximately 120k tokens and receives an independent fresh review before the next.
+
+| Phase | Reviewable result and focused proof |
+| --- | --- |
+| 1. Transactional acceptance work | Migration, scoped accepted-evidence FK/uniqueness, acceptance integration. Postgres tests prove committed accepted late power plus one work row, rollback atomicity, exact retry/duplicate/conflict/rejection, unrelated Site and zero-overlap, half-open edge, and existing migration 0011 causes/backfill. |
+| 2. Scoped drain and run plan | Role/asset/window/latest-revision recheck, typed no-op, idempotent append, claim/retry/backoff and recurring runner instructions. Test irrelevant accepted input, revised Finding between enqueue and drain, wrong Site, two workers, failure then scheduled retry, append-then-crash, restart and bounded batch; inspect exact work/attempt/consequence IDs and no duplicate basis. |
+| 3. Late-power end-to-end walkthrough | On an isolated Postgres copy of the S4-02b power fixture, first persist an exact FindingRevision and consequence, then accept a **late** good generator-power interval that changes its technical digest without relying on a new FindingRevision. Before the scheduled drain, assert `STALE/TECHNICAL_INPUT_CHANGED` and the queued work ID (or `PENDING` with work when no head); after drain, assert new consequence revision, changed accepted-evidence/technical digest, same or explicitly superseded eligible FindingRevision, old version retained, current priced eligibility for S5-01, and reload stability. Include an unrelated accepted reading that succeeds as no-op. Record commands and IDs, not illustrative mock money. |
+
+Reviewer checks migration safety, DB transaction rollback, scope/foreign Site refusal, half-open boundaries, accepted evidence identity, coarse-selection completeness, latest eligible revision, public-only lineage, no-op, retry and currentness. Run focused Postgres/API/model tests, the existing S4-02b walkthrough variant and applicable workflow guards; run `tools/check-all.ps1` when dependencies are installed. Review independently before registry resolution. No separate owner visual checkpoint is needed while this remains non-UI; S5-01 retains its own `USER_REVIEW_REQUIRED` checkpoint.
+
+Out of scope: new fuel model or price semantics, altered S4-02b copy/layout, source-authorship provenance (separate `I-stored-demo-provenance`), equal-start price succession, Assumptions Site consequence history, S5 Overview implementation, private simulator truth, and the owner's broader [analysis input data for simulated and real Sites](../.ai/MILESTONE_REVIEW_BACKLOG.md#owner-analysis-input-data-for-simulated-and-real-sites-2026-10-14) backlog item. This packet proves a late accepted input changes a consequence; it does not fix ordinary gateway power cadence or real-Site input readiness.

+# S4-02c — consequence work on accepted evidence
+
+Status: implementation-ready
+USER_REVIEW_REQUIRED: false (no new UI or owner-facing copy; independent implementation review required)
+Milestone: S4 Finding + Financials
+Depends on: merged S2-02 and reviewed/merged S4-01, S4-03, S4-02a/b; resolved `A-S4-financial` and `A-S5-overview`. S5-01's current money read depends on this packet's reviewed result.
+Branch when activated: `task/S4-02c-evidence-consequence-work`
+Planner: Codex, 2026-10-14
+
+## Outcome and authority
+
+An accepted late generator-power mean that can alter an existing Site FindingRevision's `fuel-cost-1` input creates durable consequence work in the same database transaction as acceptance. The Site read shows the old consequence as `STALE` (or `PENDING` if no consequence exists) with real queued work, then a scheduled, retryable worker derives and appends the new exact-basis consequence. The S5-01 selected-window read may use money only after that consequence is `CURRENT` and `PRICED` for its selected FindingRevision and window. A fresh stale read alone does not complete this slice.
+
+Authority: `D-2026-10-13-s4-bounded-financial-basis`, `D-2026-10-14-s402-post-review-follow-ons`, `D-2026-10-14-s5-selected-window-overview`, `.agent/architect-S4-02-batch-answers.md` Q2 and `.agent/architect-contest-2026-10-14d-answers.md` (Planner refinement). This is registry node `I-evidence-acceptance-consequence-work`, separate from S4-02a/b and S5-01's UI checkpoint.
+
+Built anchors: `.ai/CODE_STATE.md` S2-02 and S4-02b phases 1/2a/2b; `backend/assetops_backend/evidence/adapters/postgres_evidence_ledger.py` (`process_batch`/`_persist`, accepted evidence and disposition in one transaction), `backend/migrations/versions/0011_financial_consequences.py` (work, attempts and existing triggers), `backend/assetops_backend/financials/{recompute.py,consequence_read.py,adapters/postgres_consequence_store.py}`, and `backend/assetops_backend/recompute_consequences.py`. Reuse `tools/s402b_power_cases.py` and `tools/s402b_fuel_cost_walkthrough.py` as isolated fixture/walkthrough bases. The S4-02b read already detects `TECHNICAL_INPUT_CHANGED` for an unchanged FindingRevision, but acceptance currently enqueues no consequence work; its one-shot CLI has no run schedule.
+
+## Acceptance, work and worker contract
+
+1. Add a migration to extend `financial_consequence_work` with an `EVIDENCE_ACCEPTED` cause and a tenant/Site-scoped FK to the exact `accepted_evidence.id`. Keep existing assumption and FindingRevision causes and rows valid. Each new row identifies the accepted evidence, target Finding and latest eligible FindingRevision at enqueue time, and its half-open affected interval. Constrain cause shape, range, scope and a unique `(accepted_evidence_id, finding_revision_id, cause)` key; duplicates and conflicting evidence create no second row. Index pending selection by Site and due time. Preserve append-only evidence, work and attempt history. Migration upgrade/downgrade and pre-existing rows must be proved.
+2. In the S2-02 acceptance transaction, after a genuinely new accepted evidence ID is returned, select potentially affected existing Site Findings by coarse half-open interval overlap with the accepted interval and the generator-power role. Insert scoped work before commit. If the insert fails, acceptance and its disposition roll back; it must never leave a committed accepted reading with a lost required work row. Exact replay, duplicate, conflict and rejected decisions do not enqueue. If the transaction contains several accepted intervals, each exact accepted ID is deduplicated against its target. Do not trigger on a client-declared role or from a later read. Broad selection may queue a candidate that later no-ops, but must not omit a possibly affected Finding. FindingRevision insertion retains migration 0011's own trigger so findings first created after acceptance also get work.
+3. The worker treats the queued revision as a locator, then rechecks tenant/Site, accepted disposition, bound role/asset, half-open interval overlap, candidate episode/window and the **latest eligible FindingRevision** for that Finding at processing time. Derive against that exact current revision and its accepted public inputs only. A superseded or irrelevant target records a successful typed no-op; if a newer eligible revision exists, process that revision once (its insertion trigger may also queue it). No-op on unrelated roles/assets/windows without appending a consequence. A missing or closed source stays typed and retryable when transient; wrong-Site scope never falls back. Price and technical basis selection remain the reviewed S4-02b contract; no extra amount or quantity shortcut is introduced. The existing unique consequence basis and append lock must make unchanged or repeated work return the existing ID, including concurrent workers and an append-then-crash retry.
+4. Make the run plan operational: extend the server-side CLI to drain a configured tenant/Site (or a scoped active-Site iterator) on a documented one-minute recurring service/timer, with bounded batch size, a database claim/lease or equivalent single-consumer lock, persisted retry eligibility/backoff, and a restart-safe failure record. A failed item remains visible but cannot hot-loop inside one run; a later scheduled run retries it. Print/record selected, appended, replayed, no-op, failed and backlog counts with Site scope; document deployment invocation, ownership, cadence and recovery. The scheduler must not rely on a user opening Financials. Existing price/Finding work uses the same runner. A work item becomes succeeded only after all its selected targets have safely appended/replayed or no-opped; crash and concurrent-run tests must prove eventual drain without duplicate consequence basis.
+5. Keep the consequence read's `CURRENT`/`STALE`/`PENDING`/`HISTORICAL` and typed reasons. Show queued/pending status only when a real unsucceeded work row touches the selected revision; if currentness is stale but no work exists, report that discrepancy explicitly and do not claim queued. S5-01 uses only a `CURRENT`/`PRICED`, same Site/window/FindingRevision/basis consequence after work finishes. No new UI copy or mock panel is authorized here; a necessary owner-facing copy change reopens `USER_REVIEW_REQUIRED` and its checkpoint.
+

+Each phase fits one Claude Implementer context below approximately 120k tokens and receives an independent fresh review before the next.

+| 2. Scoped drain and run plan | Role/asset/window/latest-revision recheck, typed no-op, idempotent append, claim/retry/backoff and recurring runner instructions. Test irrelevant accepted input, revised Finding between enqueue and drain, wrong Site, two workers, failure then scheduled retry, append-then-crash, restart and bounded batch; inspect exact work/attempt/consequence IDs and no duplicate basis. |
+| 3. Late-power end-to-end walkthrough | On an isolated Postgres copy of the S4-02b power fixture, first persist an exact FindingRevision and consequence, then accept a **late** good generator-power interval that changes its technical digest without relying on a new FindingRevision. Include an unrelated accepted reading that succeeds as no-op. Record commands and IDs, not illustrative mock money. |

Run focused Postgres/API/model tests, the existing S4-02b walkthrough variant and applicable workflow guards; run `tools/check-all.ps1` when dependencies are installed. +# S4-02c — consequence work on accepted evidence
+
+Status: implementation-ready
+USER_REVIEW_REQUIRED: false (no new UI or owner-facing copy; independent implementation review required)
+Milestone: S4 Finding + Financials
+Depends on: merged S2-02 and reviewed/merged S4-01, S4-03, S4-02a/b; resolved `A-S4-financial` and `A-S5-overview`. S5-01's current money read depends on this packet's reviewed result.
+Branch when activated: `task/S4-02c-evidence-consequence-work`
+Planner: Codex, 2026-10-14
+
+## Outcome and authority
+
+An accepted late generator-power mean that can alter an existing Site FindingRevision's `fuel-cost-1` input creates durable consequence work in the same database transaction as acceptance. The Site read shows the old consequence as `STALE` (or `PENDING` if no consequence exists) with real queued work, then a scheduled, retryable worker derives and appends the new exact-basis consequence. The S5-01 selected-window read may use money only after that consequence is `CURRENT` and `PRICED` for its selected FindingRevision and window. A fresh stale read alone does not complete this slice.
+
+Authority: `D-2026-10-13-s4-bounded-financial-basis`, `D-2026-10-14-s402-post-review-follow-ons`, `D-2026-10-14-s5-selected-window-overview`, `.agent/architect-S4-02-batch-answers.md` Q2 and `.agent/architect-contest-2026-10-14d-answers.md` (Planner refinement). This is registry node `I-evidence-acceptance-consequence-work`, separate from S4-02a/b and S5-01's UI checkpoint.
+
+Built anchors: `.ai/CODE_STATE.md` S2-02 and S4-02b phases 1/2a/2b; `backend/assetops_backend/evidence/adapters/postgres_evidence_ledger.py` (`process_batch`/`_persist`, accepted evidence and disposition in one transaction), `backend/migrations/versions/0011_financial_consequences.py` (work, attempts and existing triggers), `backend/assetops_backend/financials/{recompute.py,consequence_read.py,adapters/postgres_consequence_store.py}`, and `backend/assetops_backend/recompute_consequences.py`. Reuse `tools/s402b_power_cases.py` and `tools/s402b_fuel_cost_walkthrough.py` as isolated fixture/walkthrough bases. The S4-02b read already detects `TECHNICAL_INPUT_CHANGED` for an unchanged FindingRevision, but acceptance currently enqueues no consequence work; its one-shot CLI has no run schedule.
+
+## Acceptance, work and worker contract
+
+1. Add a migration to extend `financial_consequence_work` with an `EVIDENCE_ACCEPTED` cause and a tenant/Site-scoped FK to the exact `accepted_evidence.id`. Keep existing assumption and FindingRevision causes and rows valid. Each new row identifies the accepted evidence, target Finding and latest eligible FindingRevision at enqueue time, and its half-open affected interval. Constrain cause shape, range, scope and a unique `(accepted_evidence_id, finding_revision_id, cause)` key; duplicates and conflicting evidence create no second row. Index pending selection by Site and due time. Preserve append-only evidence, work and attempt history. Migration upgrade/downgrade and pre-existing rows must be proved.
+2. In the S2-02 acceptance transaction, after a genuinely new accepted evidence ID is returned, select potentially affected existing Site Findings by coarse half-open interval overlap with the accepted interval and the generator-power role. Insert scoped work before commit. If the insert fails, acceptance and its disposition roll back; it must never leave a committed accepted reading with a lost required work row. Exact replay, duplicate, conflict and rejected decisions do not enqueue. If the transaction contains several accepted intervals, each exact accepted ID is deduplicated against its target. Do not trigger on a client-declared role or from a later read. Broad selection may queue a candidate that later no-ops, but must not omit a possibly affected Finding. FindingRevision insertion retains migration 0011's own trigger so findings first created after acceptance also get work.
+3. The worker treats the queued revision as a locator, then rechecks tenant/Site, accepted disposition, bound role/asset, half-open interval overlap, candidate episode/window and the **latest eligible FindingRevision** for that Finding at processing time. Derive against that exact current revision and its accepted public inputs only. A superseded or irrelevant target records a successful typed no-op; if a newer eligible revision exists, process that revision once (its insertion trigger may also queue it). No-op on unrelated roles/assets/windows without appending a consequence. A missing or closed source stays typed and retryable when transient; wrong-Site scope never falls back. Price and technical basis selection remain the reviewed S4-02b contract; no extra amount or quantity shortcut is introduced. The existing unique consequence basis and append lock must make unchanged or repeated work return the existing ID, including concurrent workers and an append-then-crash retry.
+4. Make the run plan operational: extend the server-side CLI to drain a configured tenant/Site (or a scoped active-Site iterator) on a documented one-minute recurring service/timer, with bounded batch size, a database claim/lease or equivalent single-consumer lock, persisted retry eligibility/backoff, and a restart-safe failure record. A failed item remains visible but cannot hot-loop inside one run; a later scheduled run retries it. Print/record selected, appended, replayed, no-op, failed and backlog counts with Site scope; document deployment invocation, ownership, cadence and recovery. The scheduler must not rely on a user opening Financials. Existing price/Finding work uses the same runner. A work item becomes succeeded only after all its selected targets have safely appended/replayed or no-opped; crash and concurrent-run tests must prove eventual drain without duplicate consequence basis.
+5. Keep the consequence read's `CURRENT`/`STALE`/`PENDING`/`HISTORICAL` and typed reasons. Show queued/pending status only when a real unsucceeded work row touches the selected revision; if currentness is stale but no work exists, report that discrepancy explicitly and do not claim queued. S5-01 uses only a `CURRENT`/`PRICED`, same Site/window/FindingRevision/basis consequence after work finishes. No new UI copy or mock panel is authorized here; a necessary owner-facing copy change reopens `USER_REVIEW_REQUIRED` and its checkpoint.
+
+## Phases and focused proof
+
+Each phase fits one Claude Implementer context below approximately 120k tokens and receives an independent fresh review before the next.
+
+| Phase | Reviewable result and focused proof |
+| --- | --- |
+| 1. Transactional acceptance work | Migration, scoped accepted-evidence FK/uniqueness, acceptance integration. Postgres tests prove committed accepted late power plus one work row, rollback atomicity, exact retry/duplicate/conflict/rejection, unrelated Site and zero-overlap, half-open edge, and existing migration 0011 causes/backfill. |
+| 2. Scoped drain and run plan | Role/asset/window/latest-revision recheck, typed no-op, idempotent append, claim/retry/backoff and recurring runner instructions. Test irrelevant accepted input, revised Finding between enqueue and drain, wrong Site, two workers, failure then scheduled retry, append-then-crash, restart and bounded batch; inspect exact work/attempt/consequence IDs and no duplicate basis. |
+| 3. Late-power end-to-end walkthrough | On an isolated Postgres copy of the S4-02b power fixture, first persist an exact FindingRevision and consequence, then accept a **late** good generator-power interval that changes its technical digest without relying on a new FindingRevision. Before the scheduled drain, assert `STALE/TECHNICAL_INPUT_CHANGED` and the queued work ID (or `PENDING` with work when no head); after drain, assert new consequence revision, changed accepted-evidence/technical digest, same or explicitly superseded eligible FindingRevision, old version retained, current priced eligibility for S5-01, and reload stability. Include an unrelated accepted reading that succeeds as no-op. Record commands and IDs, not illustrative mock money. |
+
+Reviewer checks migration safety, DB transaction rollback, scope/foreign Site refusal, half-open boundaries, accepted evidence identity, coarse-selection completeness, latest eligible revision, public-only lineage, no-op, retry and currentness. Run focused Postgres/API/model tests, the existing S4-02b walkthrough variant and applicable workflow guards; run `tools/check-all.ps1` when dependencies are installed. Review independently before registry resolution. No separate owner visual checkpoint is needed while this remains non-UI; S5-01 retains its own `USER_REVIEW_REQUIRED` checkpoint.
+
+Out of scope: new fuel model or price semantics, altered S4-02b copy/layout, source-authorship provenance (separate `I-stored-demo-provenance`), equal-start price succession, Assumptions Site consequence history, S5 Overview implementation, private simulator truth, and the owner's broader [analysis input data for simulated and real Sites](../.ai/MILESTONE_REVIEW_BACKLOG.md#owner-analysis-input-data-for-simulated-and-real-sites-2026-10-14) backlog item. This packet proves a late accepted input changes a consequence; it does not fix ordinary gateway power cadence or real-Site input readiness.

+# S4-02c — consequence work on accepted evidence
+
+Status: implementation-ready
+USER_REVIEW_REQUIRED: false (no new UI or owner-facing copy; independent implementation review required)
+Milestone: S4 Finding + Financials
+Depends on: merged S2-02 and reviewed/merged S4-01, S4-03, S4-02a/b; resolved `A-S4-financial` and `A-S5-overview`. S5-01's current money read depends on this packet's reviewed result.
+Branch when activated: `task/S4-02c-evidence-consequence-work`
+Planner: Codex, 2026-10-14
+
+## Outcome and authority
+
+An accepted late generator-power mean that can alter an existing Site FindingRevision's `fuel-cost-1` input creates durable consequence work in the same database transaction as acceptance. The Site read shows the old consequence as `STALE` (or `PENDING` if no consequence exists) with real queued work, then a scheduled, retryable worker derives and appends the new exact-basis consequence. The S5-01 selected-window read may use money only after that consequence is `CURRENT` and `PRICED` for its selected FindingRevision and window. A fresh stale read alone does not complete this slice.
+
+Authority: `D-2026-10-13-s4-bounded-financial-basis`, `D-2026-10-14-s402-post-review-follow-ons`, `D-2026-10-14-s5-selected-window-overview`, `.agent/architect-S4-02-batch-answers.md` Q2 and `.agent/architect-contest-2026-10-14d-answers.md` (Planner refinement). This is registry node `I-evidence-acceptance-consequence-work`, separate from S4-02a/b and S5-01's UI checkpoint.
+
+Built anchors: `.ai/CODE_STATE.md` S2-02 and S4-02b phases 1/2a/2b; `backend/assetops_backend/evidence/adapters/postgres_evidence_ledger.py` (`process_batch`/`_persist`, accepted evidence and disposition in one transaction), `backend/migrations/versions/0011_financial_consequences.py` (work, attempts and existing triggers), `backend/assetops_backend/financials/{recompute.py,consequence_read.py,adapters/postgres_consequence_store.py}`, and `backend/assetops_backend/recompute_consequences.py`. Reuse `tools/s402b_power_cases.py` and `tools/s402b_fuel_cost_walkthrough.py` as isolated fixture/walkthrough bases. The S4-02b read already detects `TECHNICAL_INPUT_CHANGED` for an unchanged FindingRevision, but acceptance currently enqueues no consequence work; its one-shot CLI has no run schedule.
+
+## Acceptance, work and worker contract
+
+1. Add a migration to extend `financial_consequence_work` with an `EVIDENCE_ACCEPTED` cause and a tenant/Site-scoped FK to the exact `accepted_evidence.id`. Keep existing assumption and FindingRevision causes and rows valid. Each new row identifies the accepted evidence, target Finding and latest eligible FindingRevision at enqueue time, and its half-open affected interval. Constrain cause shape, range, scope and a unique `(accepted_evidence_id, finding_revision_id, cause)` key; duplicates and conflicting evidence create no second row. Index pending selection by Site and due time. Preserve append-only evidence, work and attempt history. Migration upgrade/downgrade and pre-existing rows must be proved.
+2. In the S2-02 acceptance transaction, after a genuinely new accepted evidence ID is returned, select potentially affected existing Site Findings by coarse half-open interval overlap with the accepted interval and the generator-power role. Insert scoped work before commit. If the insert fails, acceptance and its disposition roll back; it must never leave a committed accepted reading with a lost required work row. Exact replay, duplicate, conflict and rejected decisions do not enqueue. If the transaction contains several accepted intervals, each exact accepted ID is deduplicated against its target. Do not trigger on a client-declared role or from a later read. Broad selection may queue a candidate that later no-ops, but must not omit a possibly affected Finding. FindingRevision insertion retains migration 0011's own trigger so findings first created after acceptance also get work.
+3. The worker treats the queued revision as a locator, then rechecks tenant/Site, accepted disposition, bound role/asset, half-open interval overlap, candidate episode/window and the **latest eligible FindingRevision** for that Finding at processing time. Derive against that exact current revision and its accepted public inputs only. A superseded or irrelevant target records a successful typed no-op; if a newer eligible revision exists, process that revision once (its insertion trigger may also queue it). No-op on unrelated roles/assets/windows without appending a consequence. A missing or closed source stays typed and retryable when transient; wrong-Site scope never falls back. Price and technical basis selection remain the reviewed S4-02b contract; no extra amount or quantity shortcut is introduced. The existing unique consequence basis and append lock must make unchanged or repeated work return the existing ID, including concurrent workers and an append-then-crash retry.
+4. Make the run plan operational: extend the server-side CLI to drain a configured tenant/Site (or a scoped active-Site iterator) on a documented one-minute recurring service/timer, with bounded batch size, a database claim/lease or equivalent single-consumer lock, persisted retry eligibility/backoff, and a restart-safe failure record. A failed item remains visible but cannot hot-loop inside one run; a later scheduled run retries it. Print/record selected, appended, replayed, no-op, failed and backlog counts with Site scope; document deployment invocation, ownership, cadence and recovery. The scheduler must not rely on a user opening Financials. Existing price/Finding work uses the same runner. A work item becomes succeeded only after all its selected targets have safely appended/replayed or no-opped; crash and concurrent-run tests must prove eventual drain without duplicate consequence basis.
+5. Keep the consequence read's `CURRENT`/`STALE`/`PENDING`/`HISTORICAL` and typed reasons. Show queued/pending status only when a real unsucceeded work row touches the selected revision; if currentness is stale but no work exists, report that discrepancy explicitly and do not claim queued. S5-01 uses only a `CURRENT`/`PRICED`, same Site/window/FindingRevision/basis consequence after work finishes. No new UI copy or mock panel is authorized here; a necessary owner-facing copy change reopens `USER_REVIEW_REQUIRED` and its checkpoint.
+
+## Phases and focused proof
+
+Each phase fits one Claude Implementer context below approximately 120k tokens and receives an independent fresh review before the next.
+
+| Phase | Reviewable result and focused proof |
+| --- | --- |
+| 1. Transactional acceptance work | Migration, scoped accepted-evidence FK/uniqueness, acceptance integration. Postgres tests prove committed accepted late power plus one work row, rollback atomicity, exact retry/duplicate/conflict/rejection, unrelated Site and zero-overlap, half-open edge, and existing migration 0011 causes/backfill. |
+| 2. Scoped drain and run plan | Role/asset/window/latest-revision recheck, typed no-op, idempotent append, claim/retry/backoff and recurring runner instructions. Test irrelevant accepted input, revised Finding between enqueue and drain, wrong Site, two workers, failure then scheduled retry, append-then-crash, restart and bounded batch; inspect exact work/attempt/consequence IDs and no duplicate basis. |
+| 3. Late-power end-to-end walkthrough | On an isolated Postgres copy of the S4-02b power fixture, first persist an exact FindingRevision and consequence, then accept a **late** good generator-power interval that changes its technical digest without relying on a new FindingRevision. Before the scheduled drain, assert `STALE/TECHNICAL_INPUT_CHANGED` and the queued work ID (or `PENDING` with work when no head); after drain, assert new consequence revision, changed accepted-evidence/technical digest, same or explicitly superseded eligible FindingRevision, old version retained, current priced eligibility for S5-01, and reload stability. Include an unrelated accepted reading that succeeds as no-op. Record commands and IDs, not illustrative mock money. |
+
+Reviewer checks migration safety, DB transaction rollback, scope/foreign Site refusal, half-open boundaries, accepted evidence identity, coarse-selection completeness, latest eligible revision, public-only lineage, no-op, retry and currentness. Run focused Postgres/API/model tests, the existing S4-02b walkthrough variant and applicable workflow guards; run `tools/check-all.ps1` when dependencies are installed. Review independently before registry resolution. No separate owner visual checkpoint is needed while this remains non-UI; S5-01 retains its own `USER_REVIEW_REQUIRED` checkpoint.
+
+Out of scope: new fuel model or price semantics, altered S4-02b copy/layout, source-authorship provenance (separate `I-stored-demo-provenance`), equal-start price succession, Assumptions Site consequence history, S5 Overview implementation, private simulator truth, and the owner's broader [analysis input data for simulated and real Sites](../.ai/MILESTONE_REVIEW_BACKLOG.md#owner-analysis-input-data-for-simulated-and-real-sites-2026-10-14) backlog item. This packet proves a late accepted input changes a consequence; it does not fix ordinary gateway power cadence or real-Site input readiness.

+# S4-02c — consequence work on accepted evidence
+
+Status: implementation-ready
+USER_REVIEW_REQUIRED: false (no new UI or owner-facing copy; independent implementation review required)
+Milestone: S4 Finding + Financials
+Depends on: merged S2-02 and reviewed/merged S4-01, S4-03, S4-02a/b; resolved `A-S4-financial` and `A-S5-overview`. S5-01's current money read depends on this packet's reviewed result.
+Branch when activated: `task/S4-02c-evidence-consequence-work`
+Planner: Codex, 2026-10-14
+
+## Outcome and authority
+
+An accepted late generator-power mean that can alter an existing Site FindingRevision's `fuel-cost-1` input creates durable consequence work in the same database transaction as acceptance. The Site read shows the old consequence as `STALE` (or `PENDING` if no consequence exists) with real queued work, then a scheduled, retryable worker derives and appends the new exact-basis consequence. The S5-01 selected-window read may use money only after that consequence is `CURRENT` and `PRICED` for its selected FindingRevision and window. A fresh stale read alone does not complete this slice.
+
+Authority: `D-2026-10-13-s4-bounded-financial-basis`, `D-2026-10-14-s402-post-review-follow-ons`, `D-2026-10-14-s5-selected-window-overview`, `.agent/architect-S4-02-batch-answers.md` Q2 and `.agent/architect-contest-2026-10-14d-answers.md` (Planner refinement). This is registry node `I-evidence-acceptance-consequence-work`, separate from S4-02a/b and S5-01's UI checkpoint.
+
+Built anchors: `.ai/CODE_STATE.md` S2-02 and S4-02b phases 1/2a/2b; `backend/assetops_backend/evidence/adapters/postgres_evidence_ledger.py` (`process_batch`/`_persist`, accepted evidence and disposition in one transaction), `backend/migrations/versions/0011_financial_consequences.py` (work, attempts and existing triggers), `backend/assetops_backend/financials/{recompute.py,consequence_read.py,adapters/postgres_consequence_store.py}`, and `backend/assetops_backend/recompute_consequences.py`. Reuse `tools/s402b_power_cases.py` and `tools/s402b_fuel_cost_walkthrough.py` as isolated fixture/walkthrough bases. The S4-02b read already detects `TECHNICAL_INPUT_CHANGED` for an unchanged FindingRevision, but acceptance currently enqueues no consequence work; its one-shot CLI has no run schedule.
+
+## Acceptance, work and worker contract
+
+1. Add a migration to extend `financial_consequence_work` with an `EVIDENCE_ACCEPTED` cause and a tenant/Site-scoped FK to the exact `accepted_evidence.id`. Keep existing assumption and FindingRevision causes and rows valid. Each new row identifies the accepted evidence, target Finding and latest eligible FindingRevision at enqueue time, and its half-open affected interval. Constrain cause shape, range, scope and a unique `(accepted_evidence_id, finding_revision_id, cause)` key; duplicates and conflicting evidence create no second row. Index pending selection by Site and due time. Preserve append-only evidence, work and attempt history. Migration upgrade/downgrade and pre-existing rows must be proved.
+2. In the S2-02 acceptance transaction, after a genuinely new accepted evidence ID is returned, select potentially affected existing Site Findings by coarse half-open interval overlap with the accepted interval and the generator-power role. Insert scoped work before commit. If the insert fails, acceptance and its disposition roll back; it must never leave a committed accepted reading with a lost required work row. Exact replay, duplicate, conflict and rejected decisions do not enqueue. If the transaction contains several accepted intervals, each exact accepted ID is deduplicated against its target. Do not trigger on a client-declared role or from a later read. Broad selection may queue a candidate that later no-ops, but must not omit a possibly affected Finding. FindingRevision insertion retains migration 0011's own trigger so findings first created after acceptance also get work.
+3. The worker treats the queued revision as a locator, then rechecks tenant/Site, accepted disposition, bound role/asset, half-open interval overlap, candidate episode/window and the **latest eligible FindingRevision** for that Finding at processing time. Derive against that exact current revision and its accepted public inputs only. A superseded or irrelevant target records a successful typed no-op; if a newer eligible revision exists, process that revision once (its insertion trigger may also queue it). No-op on unrelated roles/assets/windows without appending a consequence. A missing or closed source stays typed and retryable when transient; wrong-Site scope never falls back. Price and technical basis selection remain the reviewed S4-02b contract; no extra amount or quantity shortcut is introduced. The existing unique consequence basis and append lock must make unchanged or repeated work return the existing ID, including concurrent workers and an append-then-crash retry.
+4. Make the run plan operational: extend the server-side CLI to drain a configured tenant/Site (or a scoped active-Site iterator) on a documented one-minute recurring service/timer, with bounded batch size, a database claim/lease or equivalent single-consumer lock, persisted retry eligibility/backoff, and a restart-safe failure record. A failed item remains visible but cannot hot-loop inside one run; a later scheduled run retries it. Print/record selected, appended, replayed, no-op, failed and backlog counts with Site scope; document deployment invocation, ownership, cadence and recovery. The scheduler must not rely on a user opening Financials. Existing price/Finding work uses the same runner. A work item becomes succeeded only after all its selected targets have safely appended/replayed or no-opped; crash and concurrent-run tests must prove eventual drain without duplicate consequence basis.
+5. Keep the consequence read's `CURRENT`/`STALE`/`PENDING`/`HISTORICAL` and typed reasons. Show queued/pending status only when a real unsucceeded work row touches the selected revision; if currentness is stale but no work exists, report that discrepancy explicitly and do not claim queued. S5-01 uses only a `CURRENT`/`PRICED`, same Site/window/FindingRevision/basis consequence after work finishes. No new UI copy or mock panel is authorized here; a necessary owner-facing copy change reopens `USER_REVIEW_REQUIRED` and its checkpoint.
+
+## Phases and focused proof
+
+Each phase fits one Claude Implementer context below approximately 120k tokens and receives an independent fresh review before the next.
+
+| Phase | Reviewable result and focused proof |
+| --- | --- |
+| 1. Transactional acceptance work | Migration, scoped accepted-evidence FK/uniqueness, acceptance integration. Postgres tests prove committed accepted late power plus one work row, rollback atomicity, exact retry/duplicate/conflict/rejection, unrelated Site and zero-overlap, half-open edge, and existing migration 0011 causes/backfill. |
+| 2. Scoped drain and run plan | Role/asset/window/latest-revision recheck, typed no-op, idempotent append, claim/retry/backoff and recurring runner instructions. Test irrelevant accepted input, revised Finding between enqueue and drain, wrong Site, two workers, failure then scheduled retry, append-then-crash, restart and bounded batch; inspect exact work/attempt/consequence IDs and no duplicate basis. |
+| 3. Late-power end-to-end walkthrough | On an isolated Postgres copy of the S4-02b power fixture, first persist an exact FindingRevision and consequence, then accept a **late** good generator-power interval that changes its technical digest without relying on a new FindingRevision. Before the scheduled drain, assert `STALE/TECHNICAL_INPUT_CHANGED` and the queued work ID (or `PENDING` with work when no head); after drain, assert new consequence revision, changed accepted-evidence/technical digest, same or explicitly superseded eligible FindingRevision, old version retained, current priced eligibility for S5-01, and reload stability. Include an unrelated accepted reading that succeeds as no-op. Record commands and IDs, not illustrative mock money. |
+
+Reviewer checks migration safety, DB transaction rollback, scope/foreign Site refusal, half-open boundaries, accepted evidence identity, coarse-selection completeness, latest eligible revision, public-only lineage, no-op, retry and currentness. Run focused Postgres/API/model tests, the existing S4-02b walkthrough variant and applicable workflow guards; run `tools/check-all.ps1` when dependencies are installed. Review independently before registry resolution. No separate owner visual checkpoint is needed while this remains non-UI; S5-01 retains its own `USER_REVIEW_REQUIRED` checkpoint.
+
+Out of scope: new fuel model or price semantics, altered S4-02b copy/layout, source-authorship provenance (separate `I-stored-demo-provenance`), equal-start price succession, Assumptions Site consequence history, S5 Overview implementation, private simulator truth, and the owner's broader [analysis input data for simulated and real Sites](../.ai/MILESTONE_REVIEW_BACKLOG.md#owner-analysis-input-data-for-simulated-and-real-sites-2026-10-14) backlog item. This packet proves a late accepted input changes a consequence; it does not fix ordinary gateway power cadence or real-Site input readiness.
